issues.title: Remove @babel/core override once ecosystem no longer resolves 7.28.0
issues.description:
## Background

During a previous dependency-remediation pass, `@babel/core` was flagged for an **arbitrary file read** vulnerability (advisory `1123528`). The vulnerable peer-dependency resolution (`@babel/core@7.28.0`) was being pulled into the lockfile despite the project requesting newer versions.

The current mitigation is a combination of overrides in `package.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:

```yaml
# pnpm-workspace.yaml
peerDependencyRules:
  allowedVersions:
    '@babel/core': '>=7.29.1'

overrides:
  '@babel/core': ^7.29.7
```

```json
// package.json
"overrides": {
  "@babel/core": "^7.29.7"
}
```

These overrides force all transitive and peer consumers onto a patched version of `@babel/core`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Periodically check whether the ecosystem still pulls in `@babel/core@7.28.0` without the override (run `pnpm why @babel/core` and inspect lockfile).
- [ ] When `@babel/core` consumers have updated their peer ranges / dependency ranges so that `7.28.0` is no longer resolvable, remove the `@babel/core` overrides and `allowedVersions` entries.
- [ ] Run `pnpm install` and `pnpm audit` to confirm the override removal does not reintroduce the advisory.
- [ ] Verify the main repo CI stays green after the cleanup.

## References

* Original advisory: `1123528`
* Original remediation commit: `8c585c8f`

issues.title: Monitor and prevent reintroduction of vulnerable react-router
issues.description:
## Background

During a previous dependency-remediation pass `react-router` was flagged for an **RSC mode CSRF bypass** (advisory `1124282`). At the time, the project had no direct usage of `react-router-dom` in `src/`, so the dependency was removed and the finding was cleared from `pnpm audit`.

However, `react-router` may still be pulled transitively by other dependencies, or a future dependency update could reintroduce a vulnerable version.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirm the project still has no direct `react-router-dom` / `react-router` imports.
- [ ] Add a regression guard (e.g., `pnpm why react-router` check or a `pnpm audit` gate) to ensure no vulnerable `react-router` / `react-router-dom` version is reintroduced.
- [ ] If a patched `react-router-dom` release (`>=8.3.0` per the advisory) becomes available, evaluate re-adding it or bumping any transitive consumer.
- [ ] Once the override/removal is confirmed stable, close this issue.

## References

* Original advisory: `1124282`
* Original remediation commit: `8c585c8f`

issues.title: Remove accepted localstack risk once patched version is released
issues.description:
## Background

In a previous dependency-remediation pass we accepted `localstack` as a residual risk because pip-audit flagged it for **PYSEC-2023-243** (missing SSL verification) but no patched release was available at the time.

Current declaration in `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
# localstack is a dev/test-only dependency. pip-audit flags PYSEC-2023-243
# (missing SSL verification) but no fix version is available; accepted risk.
"localstack>=2026.5.0",
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Monitor pip-audit / PyPI for a `localstack` release that fixes PYSEC-2023-243.
- [ ] Bump `localstack` to the patched version in `pyproject.toml`.
- [ ] Run `pip-audit` to confirm the finding is cleared.
- [ ] Remove the accepted-risk comment block from `pyproject.toml` once it is no longer true.
- [ ] Run `uv sync` (or equivalent) and commit the regenerated lockfile changes.
- [ ] Verify the main repo CI stays green.

## References

* PYSEC-2023-243
* Original remediation commit: `8c585c8f`

issues.title: Remediate CVE-2026-48746 CRITICAL: bump vllm 0.20.2rc1 → ≥0.24.0 (auth bypass)
issues.description:
## CVE

* **ID:** CVE-2026-48746
* **Severity:** **CRITICAL** — authentication bypass in starlette exposed by vLLM
* **Package:** `vllm` 0.20.2rc1.dev168+gecd0b60aa.cu129 → ≥0.24.0 (bumping to 0.24.0 also clears HIGH CVEs CVE-2026-54234, CVE-2026-55514, CVE-2026-55574 in the same step)
* **Source:** Trivy filesystem scan, 2026-07-29 (`docs/linear-audit/s3-scan-results.md` §2)

## Why now (TIER 0 — only Critical)

This is the **only** CRITICAL finding from S3. The vuln is an auth bypass —
vLLM serves an internal API without auth in some configurations. Even though
vllm runs only in training/serving stack (not production web runtime), a
compromised training environment can be used to pivot to production data
pipelines. Must fix before any vendor engagement.

## Affected consumers

Source: `.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/art/_vllm_runtime/uv.lock` —
artifact runtime (ART) for vLLM-based model evaluation. Possibly also
`ai/training/`, `ai/training_data_unified/`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Identify all `uv.lock` files pinning `vllm`
- [ ] Bump `vllm` to ≥0.24.0 (clears CRITICAL + all 3 HIGH in same bump)
- [ ] Verify any training/eval pipeline that depends on vllm API surface still works
- [ ] Confirm vllm is not reachable from production network (TB4 in threat model §6)
- [ ] Re-run `trivy fs --severity CRITICAL,HIGH` to confirm CVE resolved
- [ ] Update S3 scan results doc

## Linear refs

* Parent: PIX-4137 (S3)
* Evidence: docs/linear-audit/s3-scan-results.md §2
* Threat model: docs/linear-audit/threat-model-scope.md §6 (TB4)

## Estimated effort

1 day (likely bump + training pipeline smoke test).

issues.title: Remediate pnpm audit HIGH: bump @babel/core (via @tarquinen/opencode-dcp)
issues.description:
## Audit findings

* **Source:** `pnpm audit`, 2026-07-29
* **Severity:** High (3 separate CVEs via `@babel/core`)
* **Severity tally:** 3 High + 1 Moderate + 1 Low
* **Root cause:** `@tarquinen/opencode-dcp` pins an old `@babel/core` via
  `@opencode-ai/plugin` → `@opentui/solid` → `@babel/preset-typescript`
  → `@babel/core`. 24 transitive paths.

## Why now (Tier 1)

Build-time toolchain. Lower runtime exposure than the other Tier 1 items
(API-key / JWT / framework CVEs), but a build-time RCE in `@babel/core`
can poison dist artifacts. Also blocks `pnpm audit` from being clean,
which auditors and SOC2 reviewers check.

## Tasks

- [ ] Run `pnpm why @babel/core` to confirm transitive path
- [ ] Check if `@tarquinen/opencode-dcp` has a newer release that bumps
      `@babel/core`; if yes, update `@tarquinen/opencode-dcp`
- [ ] If pinned and no upstream fix, use `pnpm.overrides` in root
      `package.json` to force a patched `@babel/core` version
- [ ] Run `pnpm install` + `pnpm build` to verify no breakage
- [ ] Re-run `pnpm audit` to confirm HIGH count drops from 3 to 0
- [ ] Update S3 scan results doc

## Linear refs

* Parent: PIX-4137 (S3)
* Evidence: docs/linear-audit/s3-scan-results.md §4

## Estimated effort

Half day (likely a one-line override).

issues.title: Quarterly Workspace Audit — Linear Hygiene Check
issues.description:
## Objective

Conduct a quarterly workspace audit to ensure Linear hygiene and identify new issues before they compound.

## Schedule

* **Frequency:** Quarterly (January, April, July, October)
* **Next audit:** 2026-10-29
* **Owner:** Chad

## Audit Procedure

### 1. Fetch Current State

```bash
cd docs/linear-audit/
python3 fetch_issues.py
```

### 2. Run Audit Analysis

```bash
python3 run_audit.py
```

### 3. Compare Against Previous Baseline

Compare output against the last `linear_audit.md` for:

* Duplicate detection (Watch for new Done-Done pairs)
* Unassigned issues (Target: 0)
* Issues without descriptions (Target: 0)
* Estimate coverage (Target: >80%)
* Assignment coverage (Target: 100%)

### 4. Apply Remediations (if needed)

```bash
python3 remediate.py
```

### 5. Update Audit Report

Save findings to `docs/linear-audit/linear_audit.md` with a new follow-up section.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All issues have descriptions
- [ ] All issues are assigned to an owner
- [ ] No Done-Done duplicate pairs exist
- [ ] Estimate coverage >80%
- [ ] Project descriptions are accurate (no inflated claims)
- [ ] Issues have been archived for completed projects
- [ ] Update linear_audit.md with findings

## Scripts Location

`docs/linear-audit/` — All audit scripts and the report document.

## History

* 2026-07-29: Initial audit and remediation completed. 20 duplicates resolved, 4 descriptions added, 146 assignments made, 149 estimates added, 7 enterprise gaps created, 15 projects archived.

issues.title: Phase 0: Meddies Synthesizer - Data Generation Pipeline
issues.description:
## Objective

Formalize the `meddies_synthesizer.py` module as an explicit PAL pipeline phase. This module generates all upstream intermediate JSONL files consumed by Phases 2.1 (selection), 2.2 (dialogue), and 3.1 (DPO).

Already delivered in the codebase at `ai/training_corpus/pal_framework/meddies_synthesizer.py` (21KB). Tests at `test_meddies_synthesizer_llm.py` (8 tests, all passing). This ticket documents and accepts it as an official project deliverable.

## Technical Capabilities

1. **Rule-based mode** (default, no API key): deterministic Vietnamese-string templates produce structurally valid records with persona-aligned content. Good for smoke tests and CI.
2. **LLM-driven mode** (`--llm` flag): persona-aware prompts sent to NVIDIA NIM (`openai/gpt-oss-120b`). Falls back to rule-based on empty/falsy LLM return.
3. **Three pipeline builders:**
   * `build_selection_input()` -> Phase 2.1: {dialogue, personas, correct_index}
   * `build_dialogue_input()` -> Phase 2.2: {persona, dialogue?, response}
   * `build_dpo_input()` -> Phase 3.1: {persona, dialogue?, chosen, rejected}
4. **Top-level runner (**`run()`**)**: Loads N records from Meddies HF dataset, adapts via `meddies_adapter`, synthesizes all three input files.
5. **CLI entry point (**`main()`**)**: `--out-dir`, `--n-records`, `--seed`, `--hf-split`, `--llm`, `--llm-model`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 8 existing synthesizer tests pass (`test_meddies_synthesizer_llm.py`).
- [ ] Rule-based mode produces valid Phase 2.1/2.2/3.1 input JSONL files with correct keys and types.
- [ ] LLM mode produces structurally valid records when an LLM client is configured.
- [ ] Empty/falsy LLM return values fall back to rule-based generation (no silent failures).
- [ ] Per-record deterministic seed derivation ensures reproducible LLM outputs for the same input record + seed pair.
- [ ] JSON serialization handles upstream datetime/date objects without TypeError.
- [ ] CLI produces non-zero exit code on invalid API key or missing args (future).
- [ ] All ruff checks pass on `meddies_synthesizer.py`.
- [ ] The `_build_llm_client_from_env()` helper wires credentials from `NVIDIA_API_KEY`, `LLM_API_KEY`, or `OPENAI_API_KEY` without error.

## Related

* Parent plan: PIX-4070 (PAL Framework Implementation Plan v2)
* Consumed by: Phase 2.1 (PIX-4072), Phase 2.2 (PIX-4073), Phase 3.1 (PIX-4074)
* Adapter dependency: `meddies_adapter.py`

## Priority

* Priority: Medium (blocking downstream; upstream pipeline is already built but undocumented)
* The rule-based pipeline runs without any API key or network access.
* LLM mode requires NVIDIA NIM credentials (`NVIDIA_API_KEY` in env).

## Delivered

Enterprise-grade hardening of the ZK Proof verification pipeline (follow-up to PIX-4068 / PIX-4069).

### Changes

`src/lib/fhe/zk-proof-service.ts`

* Added `MAX_PROOF_AGE_MS = 300_000` (5-minute freshness window) — exported constant
* Added `generateNonce()` — cryptographically-random 32-byte hex nonce per proof

issues.title: Replace hash-commitment ZK proofs with real SP1 zero-knowledge proofs
issues.description:
## Problem

PIX-4067/4068/4069 implemented a "Zero-Knowledge Proof Service" that is actually SHA-256 hash commitments, not ZK proofs. `ZKProofService.generateProof()` computes SHA-256 hashes of input/output data and builds a Merkle root. `verifyProof()` checks hash equality. This provides data integrity but NOT zero-knowledge — the prover reveals all data to the verifier, and no cryptographic proof of correct computation is generated.

ADR-0004 selected SP1 (Succinct) as the ZK library but it was never integrated. The current implementation is a placeholder that should be replaced with a production-grade ZK proof system.

## Current State

* `src/lib/fhe/zk-proof-service.ts`: Uses Web Crypto API SHA-256 + Merkle root construction
* `src/pages/api/v1/zk/verify.ts`: Verifies hash equality, not ZK proof validity
* `src/lib/fhe/__tests__/zk-benchmark.test.ts`: Benchmarks hash operations (<50ms), not actual proof generation
* ADR-0004 at `src/content-store/docs/architecture/decisions/0004-zero-knowledge-system.md` documents SP1 selection

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] SP1 guest program written in Rust that proves data pipeline integrity (input hash + operation dispatch + output hash derivation)
- [ ] `ZKProofService.generateProof()` calls SP1 prover (local or Bonsai remote) and returns a real ZK proof
- [ ] `ZKProofService.verifyProof()` calls SP1 verifier to check proof validity without revealing input data
- [ ] Proof generation completes in <10s for typical session analysis payload (1KB-100KB)
- [ ] Verification endpoint at `/api/v1/zk/verify` accepts and verifies real SP1 proofs
- [ ] Tests verify that proof generation fails when input data doesn't match the proven computation
- [ ] Tests verify that verification fails for tampered proofs
- [ ] Benchmark updated with real proof generation/verification times
- [ ] ADR-0004 updated with actual SP1 integration details
- [ ] `zk-threat-model.md` updated to reflect real ZK properties (soundness, completeness, zero-knowledge)

## Technical Notes

* SP1 requires Rust toolchain + `cargo prove` CLI
* Bonsai remote proving service available via `@risczero/bonsai-sdk` npm package
* Local proving requires GPU for sub-10s performance; CPU proving available but slower
* Guest program should prove: SHA-256(input) → operation dispatch → SHA-256(output) → Merkle root construction
* Consider GPU-proving via SP1 CUDA backend for production performance
* The existing hash-commitment logic can remain as a fallback for environments without SP1

issues.description:
## Problem

The `EvidenceGenerationService` at `src/lib/research/services/EvidenceGenerationService.ts` (758 lines) generates evidence reports with statistical findings, but the underlying statistical test computation may use placeholder logic. The `EvidenceReportGenerator` (PIX-4060) wraps this service to produce markdown reports and IRB export packages, but if the statistical tests themselves are stubs, the reports contain fabricated p-values, effect sizes, and confidence intervals.

## Current State

* `src/lib/research/services/EvidenceGenerationService.ts`: 758 lines, generates `EvidenceReport` with `findings[]` containing `StatisticalTest` results
* `StatisticalTest` type: `{ testType, variables, nullHypothesis, alternativeHypothesis, alpha, results }`
* `EvidenceReportTemplates.ts` (PIX-4060): 3 report templates with 9 hypotheses total
* `IRBExportService.ts` (PIX-4060): Generates IRB export packages from reports
* No actual statistical computation library is used (no `simple-statistics`, `ssjs`, or similar)
* Findings may contain hardcoded or randomly generated values instead of computed statistics

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Statistical test library selected and integrated (e.g., `simple-statistics` for JS, or call Python `scipy` via subprocess)
- [ ] t-test implementation for comparing two group means (intervention effectiveness)
- [ ] Chi-square test for categorical comparisons (crisis detection accuracy)
- [ ] Correlation coefficient (Pearson/Spearman) for alliance-outcome relationship
- [ ] Confidence intervals computed from actual data, not hardcoded
- [ ] p-values computed from actual test statistics, not randomly generated
- [ ] Effect sizes (Cohen's d, odds ratio) computed from actual data
- [ ] Evidence reports clearly distinguish between computed statistics and template placeholders
- [ ] Tests verify that statistical computations produce correct results for known inputs
- [ ] IRB export packages contain real statistical methodology, not placeholder text
- [ ] `EvidenceReportTemplates.ts` hypotheses connected to actual data queries (not synthetic data)

## Technical Notes

* `simple-statistics` npm package provides t-test, correlation, mean, stddev, etc.
* For more advanced tests (ANCOVA, mixed-effects), consider calling Python `scipy.stats` via subprocess
* The existing `ResearchQueryEngine` executes queries against anonymized data — statistical tests should run on query results
* `AnonymizationService` applies differential privacy noise — statistical tests must account for noise
* The 3 report templates from PIX-4060 define which tests to run:
  * Intervention effectiveness: t-test comparing technique A vs technique B outcomes
  * Crisis detection accuracy: chi-square test comparing sensitivity across time periods
  * Therapeutic alliance: Pearson correlation between alliance scores and outcome measures

issues.title: Replace FHE simulation operations with real SEAL homomorphic computation
issues.description:
## Problem

The `HomomorphicOperations` class at `src/lib/fhe/homomorphic-ops.ts` (1052 lines) claims to perform homomorphic encryption operations but actually falls back to plaintext simulation for all high-level operations. The SEAL-based operations (Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, etc.) are real, but the clinically relevant operations — SUMMARIZE, SENTIMENT, CATEGORIZE, TOKENIZE, FILTER — are local plaintext algorithms:

* `summarizeText()`: Extractive summarization (first sentences up to maxLength)
* `analyzeSentiment()`: Keyword-based positive/negative/neutral classification
* `categorizeText()`: Simple keyword matching against category lists
* `tokenizeText()`: String split by whitespace
* `filterText()`: Regex-based text filtering

The `simulateOperation()` method (line 622) decrypts data to plaintext, runs the local algorithm, then re-encrypts the result. This defeats the purpose of homomorphic encryption — patient data is exposed in plaintext during computation.

## Current State

* `src/lib/fhe/homomorphic-ops.ts`: `simulateOperation()` decrypts → local algo → re-encrypt
* SEAL config: BFV scheme, polyModulusDegree 8192, coeffModulusBits [60,40,40,40,60], plainModulus 1032193
* `ZKProofService` wraps these simulated operations with hash-commitment "proofs"
* `EmotionLlamaProvider` calls `processEncrypted()` which delegates to `simulateOperation()`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `summarizeText()` operates on ciphertext using SEAL polynomial evaluation (no decryption)
- [ ] `analyzeSentiment()` uses encrypted comparison operations or SEAL-based classifier
- [ ] `categorizeText()` uses encrypted keyword matching via SEAL multiplication
- [ ] `tokenizeText()` operates on encrypted character arrays
- [ ] `filterText()` uses encrypted comparison + conditional selection
- [ ] No plaintext intermediate values exist during computation (verified by code audit)
- [ ] Performance: each operation completes in <5s for typical session text (1KB-10KB)
- [ ] `simulateOperation()` removed or renamed to `executeOperation()` (no more "simulation")
- [ ] Tests verify that raw plaintext is never logged or exposed during operations
- [ ] ZK proofs (once upgraded) prove correct computation on encrypted data
- [ ] Documentation updated to reflect real homomorphic computation

## Technical Notes

* Microsoft SEAL via `node-seal` (WASM) is already configured
* BFV scheme supports addition, multiplication, subtraction on encrypted integers
* For text operations, encode characters as polynomial coefficients
* Sentiment analysis could use a pre-computed encrypted weight vector + SEAL multiplication
* Summarization could use encrypted similarity scoring + SEAL rotation for sentence selection
* Consider CKKS scheme for approximate arithmetic if integer BFV is insufficient
* The ZK proof issue (parent PIX-3927) should be resolved in parallel — real FHE + real ZK proofs together provide the intended security guarantee

issues.title: Persist ConsentManagementService to PostgreSQL + Redis (replace in-memory store)
issues.description:
## Problem

The ConsentManagementService at `src/lib/research/services/ConsentManagementService.ts` (443 lines) stores all consent records, audit logs, and withdrawal data in-memory using `Map` and array data structures. When the server restarts, all consent state is lost. The ConsentExpiryService (PIX-4058) correctly identifies expiring consents but reads from the same in-memory store, meaning expiry checks only work within a single server lifecycle.

This is not HIPAA-compliant for production: consent records must be durably persisted with 7-year retention (2555 days per HIPAA §164.530(j)).

## Current State

* `src/lib/research/services/ConsentManagementService.ts`: In-memory `Map<string, ConsentRecord>` + `ConsentAuditLog[]` array
* `src/lib/consent/ConsentExpiryService.ts`: Reads from in-memory store
* 6 API routes at `src/pages/api/v1/admin/consent/` delegate to the in-memory service
* No database schema for consent records exists

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] PostgreSQL schema created for consent records (table: `consent_records`) with columns matching `ConsentRecord` type
- [ ] PostgreSQL schema created for consent audit trail (table: `consent_audit_trail`) with 7-year retention policy
- [ ] `ConsentManagementService` refactored to use PostgreSQL via existing `query` from `@/lib/db`
- [ ] Redis used for hot-path reads (consent level lookups) with write-through to PostgreSQL
- [ ] Consent expiry service reads from PostgreSQL (works across restarts)
- [ ] All 6 existing API routes work unchanged (same interface, durable storage)
- [ ] Migration script created at `db/migrations/013_consent_records.sql` with rollback
- [ ] Tests updated to mock PostgreSQL + Redis (matching existing `developer-api-keys.test.ts` pattern)
- [ ] Existing consent-management.astro dashboard works with persisted data
- [ ] Audit trail survives server restart

## Technical Notes

* Existing DB pattern: `query` from `src/lib/db/index.ts`, mock pattern in `developer-api-keys.test.ts`
* Redis pattern: `LegacyRedisClient` from `src/lib/redis.ts` with `setex`/`hset`/`hgetall`
* The existing `src/lib/security/consent/ConsentService.ts` has a MongoDB-backed stub that could be referenced for schema design
* `CONSENT_TABLES` constant in `src/lib/security/consent/types.ts` lists table names
* HIPAA retention: 7 years (2555 days) per §164.530(j)(1)

issues.title: Bias Detection Engine Overhaul — Consolidation + Real Detection
issues.description:
## Goal

Fixed and completed. The bias detection engine is split across four loosely-coupled surfaces that disagree on taxonomy, rely on mock/random scores, and return placeholder constants. This overhaul consolidates vocabulary, replaces mock scores with real detection, wires or removes placeholder services, and establishes a unified engine substrate — without inventing new vocabulary (uses the existing 17-value `BiasType` enum as canonical).

## Background

Four surfaces detected in audit:

1. **Standalone Python regex** — `ai-services/security/bias_detector.py` (3-string categories: gender/age/ethnicity/language)
2. **TS orchestrator** — `src/lib/ai/bias-detection/BiasDetectionEngine.ts` with 4-layer weighted average (`BiasLayerWeights` at `types.ts:41-46`) delegating to Python HTTP service; `OptimizedBiasDetectionService` persists/caches; HIPAA-masks demographics
3. **Python service** — `src/lib/ai/bias-detection/python-service/` Flask + placeholder-heavy analyzer (`services/bias_detection_service.py:99-128` runs 6 hardcoded layers, most routing to `placeholder_service.py` constants)
4. **Pipeline shims** — `ai/api/techdeck_integration/communication/bias_integration.py` (4 `_analyze_*` methods return `random.uniform(...)` mock scores, lines 218-403) + `ai/safety/bias_privacy_hooks.py`

Conflicting taxonomy vocabularies (5 surfaces):

* `deslop` `DEFAULT_RULE_PACKS` — 10 named collections
* Local detector — 3-string categories
* TechDeck `BiasType` — 8-value enum (`ai/api/techdeck_integration/integration/bias_detection.py:26-36`)
* python-service `BiasType` — 17-value enum (`python-service/bias_detection/models.py:11-30`)
* `constants.py:84` — 4-value `BIASED_TERMS_DICT`

Heavy ML deps declared in `python-service/requirements.txt` (`tensorflow`, `torch`, `transformers`, `spacy`, `scikit-learn`, `aif360`, `fairlearn`) but most code paths route to placeholder services returning constants or `random.uniform`.

## Success State (explicit, verifiable)

1. **Consolidated taxonomy:** The 4 vocabulary surfaces mapped and consolidated. The 17-value `BiasType` (`GENDER`, `RACIAL`, `AGE`, `RELIGIOUS`, `SOCIOECONOMIC`, `ABILITY`, `SEXUAL_ORIENTATION`, `POLITICAL`, `GEOGRAPHIC`, `LANGUAGE`, `EDUCATIONAL`, `HEALTH`, `APPEARANCE`, `FAMILY_STATUS`, `VETERAN_STATUS`, `IMMIGRATION`, `CRIMINAL_HISTORY`) is canonical.
2. **No mock/random scores:** All `random.uniform(...)` in `bias_integration.py` removed or replaced with real lexical/ML detection. All `placeholder_service.fairlearn_placeholder_predictions()` (deterministic parity `1 if (i+feature_sum)%2==0 else 0`) and `interpreter_placeholder_analysis()` (`bias_score: 0.25`) either wired to `fairlearn`/`aif360` or removed.
3. **No placeholder-only paths:** The 6 layer names in `services/bias_detection_service.py:99-128` either have real implementations or are documented as removed.
4. **Real fallback, not fake score:** `BiasDetectionEngine.ts:287-289` (`biasScore: 0.5 / confidence: 0.4` on service failure) preserved as documented contract — not hidden, not random.
5. **Engine substrate:** `packages/deslop/deslop/models.py` (`Finding`, `ScanReport`) extended with `category` field drawn from 17-enum. `RuleSet` extended with `bias` pack (port from `bias_detector.py:71-87`), `sycophancy` (lexical agreement-farming), `fabrication-signal` (fake-citation, over-precise numbers — lexical only, no truth-oracle claim).
6. **Dependency fix:** `packages/deslop/pyproject.toml` declares `typer` (currently imported at `cli.py:3` but missing from deps).
7. **Input/output contracts unified:** One `TherapeuticSession` / `BiasAnalysisResult` definition (Pydantic `python-service/` as source; TS `types.ts` derived).
8. **Custom rules / YAML pack support preserved:** Merged engine retains `deslop`'s YAML-config (`load_rule_set`) mechanism for user-defined markers.

## Risk / Constraints

* `fairlearn==0.13.0` / `aif360==0.6.1` declared in `requirements.txt`; audit must verify they're actually imported (`services/fairness_analyzer.py` has lazy-load branches that may fall back to placeholder). If not importable, the fairlearn-layer real-detection path must fall back to lexical-only rules.
* Taxonomy mapping: `language` (local) → `LANGUAGE`; `racial` ([constants.py](<http://constants.py>)) → `RACIAL`; `ethnicity` (local) → `RACIAL` (plan reviewer confirms — split if needed); `gender` → `GENDER`; `age` → `AGE`; `ability` → `ABILITY`.
* No suppression comments (`# noqa` / `# type: ignore`) used. No secrets in fixtures. `deslop` `pyproject.toml` `typer` gap is a real dependency, not cosmetic.
* SLA: mental-health context — flagging a user's genuine writing as "AI" (future detector A) is a harm. This epic scopes detectors to auditing our own assistant behavior + known conversation logs, not open-world AI-text detection.

## Sub-issues (5 — to be created and linked)

1. **Taxonomy Reconciliation** — Reconcile 4 bias vocabulary surfaces into 17-value `BiasType` enum (label `taxonomy`, priority High)
2. **Mock-score Removal** — Remove `random.uniform(...)` shims from `bias_integration.py` + `bias_privacy_hooks.py` (priority Critical)
3. **Placeholder Replacement** — Wire or remove placeholder fairness/interpretability layers (priority Critical)
4. **Engine Substrate + Detection Contract** — Extend `deslop` `RuleSet`/`Finding` with `bias`/`sycophancy`/`fabrication-signal` categories; fix `pyproject.toml` `typer` (priority High)
5. **Dependency Audit + Final Report** — Audit ML deps, remove install-bloat, deliver `BIAS_CONSOLIDATION_REPORT.md` (priority Medium)

Full plan in repo: `/home/vivi/pixelated/LINEAR_PLAN.md`

issues.title: PAL Framework Implementation Plan
issues.description:
# 🚀 PAL Framework Implementation Plan (v2)

## 🎯 Goal

Implement the **Persona-Aware Alignment (PAL)** framework (arxiv:2511.10215v1) using the `Meddies/meddies-persona-vie` dataset as our foundational persona repository. The ultimate objective is to train our models to **strictly adhere to complex patient personas** across demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical dimensions, moving beyond generic Next-Token Prediction (NTP) to explicit Persona Alignment via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).

---

## 📋 Context & Constraints

* **Dataset:** 150,000 synthetic Vietnamese patient records from `Meddies/meddies-persona-vie`.
* **Objective:** Replace generic model responses with highly specific, persona-aligned dialogue.
* **Core Mechanisms:** Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) followed by Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).

---

## 🛠️ Implementation Phases

### 🟩 Phase 1: Natural Language Persona Prompting (COMPLETED ✅)

*We need to translate dense JSON Meddies records into fluid, natural language strings that the LLM can interpret organically.*

* **\[x\] Task 1.1: Build Extraction Pipeline**
  * Created `ai/training_corpus/pal_framework/meddies_to_pal.py`.
  * Extracts demographics, healthcare behavior, and LLM-facing fields.
  * Formats into a clean paragraph (e.g., *"This patient is a 45-year-old female from Hanoi with low health literacy..."*).
* **\[x\] Task 1.2: Validation & Testing**
  * Created `tests/utils/test_pal_persona_formatting.py`.
  * Validated that absolutely **no JSON formatting, brackets, or quotes leak** into the natural language output.

### 🟨 Phase 2: Persona-Aware Learning (SFT Stage)

*Implement the mixed-task Supervised Fine-Tuning pipeline defined in the PAL paper.*

* **\[ \] Task 2.1: Dialogue-Informed Persona Selection (Task 1)**
  * **Objective:** Train the model to deduce a persona from dialogue.
  * **Action:** Generate synthetic dialogue using a specific persona. Create prompts asking the model to select the correct persona from a list of 3-4 distractors.
  * **File:** `ai/training_corpus/pal_framework/generate_selection_dataset.py`
* **\[ \] Task 2.2: Persona-Enhanced Dialogue Generation (Task 2)**
  * **Objective:** Train the model to roleplay the persona.
  * **Action:** Construct standard prompts: *"Given this persona: \[Meddies NL string\] and this dialogue history, generate the next response."*
  * **File:** `ai/training_corpus/pal_framework/generate_sft_dialogue.py`
* **\[ \] Task 2.3: Dry-Run SFT Validation**
  * Generate a unified 10,000-record mixed-task JSONL file.
  * Validate output against strict ChatML formatting requirements.

### 🟧 Phase 3: Persona Alignment (DPO Stage)

*Construct preference pairs to explicitly penalize out-of-character or generic generations.*

* **\[ \] Task 3.1: Construct Preference Pairs**
  * **Action:** Build `ai/training_corpus/pal_framework/generate_dpo_pairs.py`.
  * **Chosen ($y_w$):** The generated response that adheres to the persona (e.g., uses appropriate dialect, respects low health literacy).
  * **Rejected ($y_l$):** A contrasting response that violates the persona (e.g., uses high medical jargon for a low-literacy patient, ignores a cultural health bias).
* **\[ \] Task 3.2: Formatting & Linting**
  * Ensure the dataset strictly complies with the standard HuggingFace `trl` DPO format (`prompt`, `chosen`, `rejected`).

### 🟥 Phase 4: Integration & Training

*Wire the datasets into the main Lightning/Torch pipeline for actual training.*

* **\[ \] Task 4.1: Model Pipeline Integration**
  * Wire the generated SFT and DPO datasets into the existing Torch training loop.
* **\[ \] Task 4.2: Inference Wrapper**
  * Define a "Select then Generate" inference wrapper for production use, forcing the model to select a persona before generating the final response.

---

## 🔗 Links & Resources

* **Paper Reference:** [PAL: Persona-Aware Alignment](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10215v1>)
* **Dataset Repo:** `Meddies/meddies-persona-vie`
* **Target Directory:** `ai/training_corpus/pal_framework/`

issues.title: Foresight MCP: SQLite → Postgres-Only Migration
issues.description:
## Summary

Migrate Foresight MCP from dual-store (SQLite + Postgres) to **Postgres-only**. Eliminate silent SQLite fallback that causes dual-write data drift across the 3-machine fleet (sinker/billy/gnasty). No fallback. Fail-fast at startup if `FORESIGHT_DB_URL` is unset. Tests keep SQLite for speed (per `mgmt/mgmt ab61f63e58` real-world migration pattern).

## Problem (the dual-store bug)

The daemon silently splits writes between local SQLite (`~/.foresight/memory.db`) and shared Ghost Postgres depending on which code path fires. Symptoms confirmed:

* SQLite: 20 memories, last write 2026-07-03 (stale)
* Postgres (Ghost): 9 memories, all new SSE-server writes (current)
* `foresight status` → 9 (uses `_initialize_backend()` → Postgres)
* `foresight list` → empty (CLI config only has `db_path`, plus `search_memories` returns a formatted string but CLI checks `isinstance(result, list)`)

Root causes:

* `server.py:862` `_initialize_backend()` silently no-ops when `FORESIGHT_DB_URL` is unset
* `backend_factory.py:53` `create_backend()` returns `SqliteBackend` when no URL
* 22 source modules call `get_pool()` directly (bypass `get_db_connection()` routing)
* `OperationQueue` writes to its own `~/.foresight/operations.db` SQLite file
* `NarrativeCache` writes to its own `~/.foresight/narrative_cache.sqlite` file

## Surface Area

**599 grep matches across 38 source + 30 test files.**

Top coupled files: `server.py` (28), `narrative_cache.py` (20), `eval_harness.py` (18), `graph_store.py` (17), `sqlite_backend.py` (14), `decay_model.py` (13), `temporal_service.py` (11), `sync.py` (11), `auth.py` (10), `hooks.py` (7).

## Architecture Decisions AD1-AD9 (Oracle-confirmed ✅)

* **AD1**: `get_pool()` becomes routing shim + `_PsycopgPoolAdapter` (psycopg has no `acquire()`/`release()` — adapter wraps `connection()` CM). `PostgresPooledConnection` (server.py:402-480) already provides the PooledConnection shape w/ SQL translation. 22 callers untouched.
* **AD2**: Remove silent fallback in `_initialize_backend()` line 862 → `raise RuntimeError`.
* **AD3**: Remove `SqliteBackend` branch in `backend_factory.create_backend()` line 53 → `raise RuntimeError`.
* **AD4**: Keep `SqliteBackend` as test-only fixture (per mgmt/mgmt pattern). ADD nightly Postgres-backed smoke matrix.
* **AD5**: Migrate `operations` table into main Postgres as v12 migration. Drop `~/.foresight/operations.db`.
* **AD6**: Migrate `narrative_cache` table into main Postgres as v12. Drop `~/.foresight/narrative_cache.sqlite`. Delete `_harden_file_permissions`.
* **AD7**: CLI `CliConfig` `db_path` → `db_url`, ENV_MAP `FORESIGHT_DB_PATH` → `FORESIGHT_DB_URL`, `~/.foresight/config.json` replace `db_path` w/ Postgres URL on 3 machines.
* **AD8**: Fix `foresight list` empty bug — `search_memories()` returns string, CLI checks `isinstance(list)`, falls to `out.print_json` silent no-op. Use `list_memories()` instead.
* **AD9**: Keep psycopg pool `open=True`. Bump `min_size=2, max_size=10` → `max_size=20` (Oracle Q3 said max=10 too low for SSE bursts).

## Migration Phases (each shippable independently)

* **Phase 1**: Pool adapter scaffold + `get_pool()` routing + fail-fast fallback removal + pool sizing bump. Verify: pytest + daemon + `foresight status`.
* **Phase 2**: Migrate `OperationQueue` + `NarrativeCache` into Postgres via v12 schema migration. Drop standalone SQLite files. Verify: pytest + e2e + `SELECT count FROM operations; narrative_cache`.
* **Phase 3**: CLI `db_url` + `foresight list` bug. Deploy `~/.foresight/config.json` to 3 machines. Verify: `foresight list` returns rows on all 3.
* **Phase 4**: Cleanup — version bump 0.18.1 → 0.19.0, CHANGELOG, README Postgres-only, AGENTS.md note.

## Risks (top 3 of 10)

1. `~~psycopg_pool~~`~~ lacks ~~`~~acquire/release~~`~~ parity~~ — **RESOLVED**: `_PsycopgPoolAdapter` (AD1).
2. **NEW**: Large `BLOB`→`BYTEA` truncation (PG ~256MB limit). Add pre-migration scan + soft limit.
3. **NEW**: PG TXID wraparound from long-running transactions. Audit all `commit()`/`rollback()` paths. Add transaction-duration metric.

## Plan Document

**Full plan:** `/home/vivi/pixelated/.omo/plans/sqlite-to-postgres-migration.md` (12 sections, Oracle review complete, pending Momus review).

## Acceptance Criteria

* `foresight list` returns 9 rows on all 3 machines (sinker/billy/gnasty)
* `foresight store "X" --category test` from all 3 machines shows up in `SELECT count(*) FROM memories` on Ghost
* `~/.foresight/memory.db`, `~/.foresight/operations.db`, `~/.foresight/narrative_cache.sqlite` all absent or unused after Phase 2
* Daemon refuses to start without `FORESIGHT_DB_URL` with a clear error message
* `pytest` full suite green
* `psql ... -c "SELECT count(*) FROM operations; SELECT count(*) FROM narrative_cache"` returns counts
* One-click rollback: `git revert <phase-commit> && systemctl --user restart foresight-mcp` on all 3 machines

## Status

* ✅ Research complete (web + psycopg docs)
* ✅ Surface area mapped (599 matches / 68 files)
* ✅ Plan document written (`.omo/plans/sqlite-to-postgres-migration.md`)
* ✅ Oracle review complete — all 9 ADs confirmed, 6 open questions resolved
* 🔄 Linear ticket created (this issue)
* ⏳ Momus review pending
* ⏳ Implementation Phase 1 (pending Momus pass)

issues.title: Fireworks AI provider + tier-aware rate limiter (Fireworks / NVIDIA / OpenAI)
issues.description:
Phase 7 (PIX-3996) Neon provisioning is paused on `staging`. This ticket forks the work to add Fireworks AI to the LLM facade (`ai/utils/common/llm_client.py`) and add a tier-aware rate-limiter middleware so the agent and AI service stay within Fireworks starter-tier TPM caps.

**Scope**

1. **Add** `FireworksDriver` to `ai/utils/common/llm_client.py`. Reuse the OpenAI-SDK with base URL `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1` — Fireworks exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so a thin subclass that overrides the `base_url` and routes to a Fireworks-specific entry is sufficient.
2. **Add tier-aware token-bucket rate-limiter middleware** to `LLMClient` covering all three paths: Fireworks, NVIDIA NIM, OpenAI. Bucket scoped per `(provider, account, model)` — matches Fireworks' rule "Rate limits are scoped per account and per model."
3. **Tier source-of-truth** (in priority order):
   * Env override wins: `FIREWORKS_API_TIER`, `NVIDIA_API_TIER`, `OPENAI_TIER` (literal tier name).
   * On Fireworks only, if env var absent: GET `https://api.fireworks.ai/v1/accounts/me` with TTL cache (default 1h).
   * NVIDIA and OpenAI use static tier tables only.
4. **Starter-tier defaults** (the tier this same OpenCode session runs on, per Fireworks rate-limits doc):
   * 3.6M Total Prompt TPM / 900K Uncached Prompt TPM / 36K Generated TPM.
   * Track from response headers: `X-Ratelimit-Limit-Tokens-Prompt`, `X-Ratelimit-Limit-Tokens-Cache-Adjusted-Prompt`, `X-Ratelimit-Limit-Tokens-Generated`.

**Files touched**

* `ai/utils/common/llm_client.py` — add `FireworksDriver`, add `TierAwareRateLimiter`, wire it into `LLMClient.generate`.
* `ai/utils/common/rate_limiter.py` — new token-bucket implementation + tier-resolution helper.
* `ai/utils/common/tier_tables.py` — new static tier tables for NVIDIA / OpenAI.
* `ai/utils/common/tests/test_rate_limiter.py` — unit tests.
* `ai/utils/common/tests/test_llm_client.py` — extend with middleware integration.
* `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_PIX-XXXX_fireworks_rate_limit.md` (root) — design doc.

**Verification**

* `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` (or `uv run ruff` / `uv run pyright`).
* `uv run pytest ai/utils/common/tests/`.
* One live Fireworks call to confirm header parsing.
* One back-pressure test to confirm 429 retries with exponential backoff.

**Out of scope** (stays in PIX-3996): Neon provisioning, Redis companion, multi-agent memory sharing, DEPLOYMENT.md.

Build FHE performance benchmark suite and regression tests
issues.description:
## Context

The performance review (PIX-1896) found that FHE emotion classification is 2-10x slower than plaintext classification. Without benchmarks, we have no way to:

* Measure the impact of optimizations (e.g., slot packing)
* Detect performance regressions before they ship
* Set realistic latency SLOs for clinical AI conversations

## Deliverables

### 1. Benchmark Suite (`src/lib/fhe/__tests__/fhe-benchmark.test.ts`)

Create a comprehensive benchmark suite that measures:

**Latency Benchmarks**

* `encrypt()` latency: measure single-text encryption time (ms)
* `decrypt()` latency: measure single-text decryption time (ms)
* `processEncrypted()` latency: measure homomorphic operation time (ms)
* `classify()` end-to-end latency: encrypt → process → decrypt for single text
* `classifyBatch(N)` latency: end-to-end for batch sizes N = [1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500]
* `sessionTrajectory()` latency: for session with N messages

**Throughput Benchmarks**

* Texts per second (classifyBatch throughput at various batch sizes)
* Comparison: FHE vs plaintext (same operation without FHE)
* Scaling curve: batch size vs total time (should be sublinear with slot packing)

**Memory Benchmarks**

* Heap usage during classifyBatch(100)
* Ciphertext size vs plaintext size ratio

**Reliability Benchmarks**

* p99 latency over 100 runs (not just averages)
* Error rate under load (concurrency stress test)

### 2. Integration with CI

Add benchmark results to the test output and compare against stored baselines:

```typescript
// src/lib/fhe/__tests__/fhe-benchmark.test.ts
import { benchmarkReport } from '@/test/benchmark-reporter';

describe('FHE Performance Benchmarks', () => {
  it('classify() should complete within 200ms', async () => {
    const result = await benchmark('FHE.classify()', () => classifier.classify('I feel great today'));
    expect(result.durationMs).toBeLessThan(200);
  });

  it('classifyBatch(10) should complete within 1500ms', async () => {
    const texts = Array(10).fill('I feel great today');
    const result = await benchmark('FHE.classifyBatch(10)', () => classifier.classifyBatch(texts));
    expect(result.durationMs).toBeLessThan(1500);
  });
});
```

### 3. Plaintext Baseline Comparison

Add parallel benchmarks for `EmotionClassifier` (plaintext) so we can compute the FHE overhead ratio:

* FHE overhead = FHE latency / Plaintext latency
* Track this ratio over time to detect increases

### 4. Performance SLOs

Establish explicit SLOs in code:

```typescript
// src/lib/fhe/performance.ts
export const PERFORMANCE_SLOS = {
  classify_MAX_MS: 200,
  classifyBatch10_MAX_MS: 1500,
  classifyBatch50_MAX_MS: 5000,
  FHE_OVERHEAD_MAX_RATIO: 10,  // FHE should be no more than 10x plaintext
};
```

### 5. Regression Detection

Use the benchmark reporter to fail CI if:

* Any benchmark exceeds its SLO
* FHE overhead ratio increases by >20% vs baseline
* Latency p99 increases by >30% vs baseline

## Files to Create/Modify

* `src/lib/fhe/__tests__/fhe-benchmark.test.ts` (new)
* `src/lib/fhe/performance.ts` (new — SLO constants)
* `src/lib/test/benchmark-reporter.ts` (new — reusable benchmark framework)
* `src/lib/memory/__tests__/emotion-classifier.test.ts` — add plaintext benchmarks for baseline comparison

## Metrics to Track Over Time

Store benchmark results in a JSON artifact or append to a CSV. Graph over time:

* `classify` p50/p95/p99 latency (ms)
* `classifyBatch` throughput (texts/sec)
* FHE overhead ratio vs plaintext
* Ciphertext size (bytes) vs plaintext size ratio

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All benchmark tests run in CI and fail if SLOs are violated
- [ ] Baseline metrics are stored and compared against new results on each run
- [ ] Both FHE and plaintext benchmarks exist for comparison
- [ ] Benchmark suite runs in <5 minutes total

issues.title: Security audit: Find and fix unprotected JSON.parse calls across codebase
issues.description:
## Context

`JSON.parse()` on untrusted input is a medium-severity security finding. While the FHE target files (`fhe-emotion-classifier.ts`, `mock-fhe-service.ts`, `seal-context.ts`) were wrapped with input validation, the verification agent noted that unprotected `JSON.parse` calls likely exist elsewhere in the broader codebase.

`JSON.parse` with untrusted input can lead to:

* **Prototype pollution** (e.g., `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"admin":true}}')`)
* **Denial of service** (deeply nested JSON causing stack overflow)
* **Unexpected type coercion** if the parsed result is used without type checking

## Scope of Audit

Search the entire codebase for `JSON.parse(` (any variation) and evaluate each call:

### High-Risk Patterns (must fix)

* `JSON.parse(userInput)` where `userInput` comes from HTTP requests, database, or external APIs
* `JSON.parse` without subsequent type validation
* `JSON.parse` in security-sensitive contexts (auth, encryption, tenant routing)

### Medium-Risk Patterns (should fix)

* `JSON.parse` in service layers without try/catch
* `JSON.parse` on data that crosses trust boundaries (e.g., data from other microservices)

### Low-Risk Patterns (document if exempt)

* `JSON.parse` on hardcoded strings (config files, test fixtures)
* `JSON.parse` on data already validated by a trusted upstream service

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Discover (1 day)

Run grep/agent search across entire codebase:

```
JSON.parse(
JSON.parse(
```

For each file found, determine:

* Source of the input (trusted or untrusted?)
* What happens with the parsed result
* Whether there's already a try/catch
* Whether type validation exists downstream

### Step 2: Categorize findings (1 day)

Create a spreadsheet记录 of all `JSON.parse` calls with:

* File + line number
* Input source (user/untrusted or internal/trusted)
* Risk level (HIGH/MED/LOW)
* Current protection (try/catch? type guard? validation?)
* Owner (which team/file owns this code)

### Step 3: Fix high-risk findings (2-3 days)

For each HIGH-risk finding:

1. Add try/catch with appropriate error handling
2. Add schema validation (use `zod` or `joi` if already in use, otherwise plain type guards)
3. Add security test case

### Step 4: Fix medium-risk findings (2-3 days)

Same pattern as Step 3 for MED-risk.

### Step 5: Document LOW-risk as accepted (1 day)

For LOW-risk `JSON.parse` on hardcoded/internal data, document the exemption in code comments.

## Files Likely to Need Review

Based on common patterns across the codebase, likely candidates include:

* `src/lib/tenant/` — tenant data loading
* `src/lib/session/` — session parsing
* `src/lib/auth/` — token/credential parsing
* `src/lib/fhe/` — already audited but double-check
* `src/lib/memory/` — emotion/pattern data loading
* Any `*.config.ts` files that load JSON configs

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All HIGH-risk `JSON.parse` calls have try/catch AND type validation
- [ ] All MED-risk `JSON.parse` calls have try/catch
- [ ] All LOW-risk `JSON.parse` calls are documented as exempt or fixed
- [ ] No `JSON.parse` call silently swallows errors without logging
- [ ] New code added after this audit follows the same validation pattern

## Context

`fhe-factory.ts` contains an inline stub tenant manager (`_createMinimalTenantManager`) at around line 408-430. The codebase has a full `tenant-manager.ts` implementation that is not being used.

**Current state**: FHE factory uses its own minimal inline implementation for tenant validation and service limits.

**Desired state**: Use the production `TenantManager` from `src/lib/tenant/tenant-manager.ts` (or wherever it lives), which handles:

* Tenant lifecycle (creation, archival, deletion)

## Why This Matters

* **Security**: The inline stub may not enforce production tenant policies (key rotation schedules, data residency, access controls)
* **Maintenance**: Duplicate tenant management logic creates divergence risk
* **Compliance**: HIPAA clinical data requires auditable tenant isolation — the inline stub may not have the necessary audit trail
* **Feature gap**: The real `TenantManager` likely has capabilities the inline stub lacks (e.g., per-tenant FHE key rotation, tenant-level rate limiting)

## Investigation Required

Before implementing, investigate:

1. Where is `tenant-manager.ts` located and what does its interface look like?
2. Does it have the methods the FHE factory needs (or can it be extended)?
3. Does it support async initialization needed for FHE service setup?
4. Are there circular dependency concerns?

## Implementation Approach

### Option A: Direct wiring (Recommended if interface is compatible)

Replace the inline stub with an imported `TenantManager` instance. Update `getTenantFHEService()` to call real tenant validation.

```typescript
import { TenantManager } from '@/lib/tenant/tenant-manager';

private tenantManager = TenantManager.getInstance();

async getTenantFHEService(tenantId: string): Promise<FHEService> {
  await this.tenantManager.validateTenant(tenantId);  // throws if invalid
  // ...
```

### Option B: Adapter pattern (if interface mismatch)

Create a thin `TenantManagerAdapter` that wraps `TenantManager` and exposes the interface the FHE factory expects, without modifying the real `TenantManager`.

- [ ] All existing FHE tests pass with real `TenantManager`

issues.title: Implement true FHE batching via SEAL slot packing for classifyBatch
issues.description:
## Context

`FHEEmotionClassifier.classifyBatch()` currently processes texts **one at a time**: for each text it calls `encrypt → processEncrypted → decrypt`. For a batch of 10 texts, this results in **20 separate FHE operations** (10 encrypt + 10 decrypt).

This is 2-10x slower than plaintext classification (measured in performance review).

## Problem

Current `classifyBatch`:

```typescript
const results = await Promise.all(
  texts.map(async (text) => {
    const encrypted = await fheService.encrypt(text);
    const opResult = await fheService.processEncrypted(encrypted, op);
    const decrypted = await fheService.decrypt(opResult);
    return JSON.parse(decrypted);
  })
);
```

This is **not true batching**. Each item goes through the full encrypt→process→decrypt pipeline independently.

## Solution: SEAL Slot Packing

Most FHE schemes (including SEAL/BFV used here) support **slot packing** — packing multiple values into a single ciphertext and performing bulk homomorphic operations in a single `processEncrypted` call.

For a BFV scheme with polyModulusDegree 8192, you can store ~4096 Int32 values in a single ciphertext slot. This means processing a batch of 4096 texts costs the same as processing 1 text in terms of homomorphic compute.

## Implementation Roadmap

### Phase 1: Investigate SEAL slot packing support (1-2 days)

* Read SEAL documentation for `encodeBatch()` / `decodeBatch()` in `seal-service.ts`
* Verify the BFV parameters in `seal-context.ts` support slot packing (polyModulusDegree must be large enough)
* Check if `processEncrypted` in `RealFHEService` can accept batch-encoded inputs

### Phase 2: Design the batch encryption interface (1 day)

```typescript
interface BatchEncryptedData {
  data: Uint8Array;      // Slot-packed ciphertext
  metadata: {
    count: number;       // Number of texts packed
    originalLengths: number[];  // For variable-length texts
  };
}
```

### Phase 3: Implement batch encrypt/decrypt in RealFHEService (3-5 days)

* Add `encryptBatch(texts: string[]): Promise<BatchEncryptedData>`
* Add `decryptBatch(batch: BatchEncryptedData): Promise<string[]>`
* Modify `processEncrypted` to handle `BatchEncryptedData`

### Phase 4: Update FHEEmotionClassifier to use batching (2 days)

* Replace per-item encrypt→process→decrypt with batch calls
* Handle truncation (pad last batch if count < slot capacity)
* Add `BATCH_SLOT_SIZE` constant (e.g., 4096 for polyModulusDegree 8192)

### Phase 5: Benchmark and validate (2 days)

* Measure end-to-end latency for batches of size 1, 10, 50, 100, 1000
* Verify accuracy matches per-item processing
* Validate with mock service

## Expected Performance Impact

| Batch Size | Current (ms) | Target with Slot Packing (ms) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | ~50 | ~50 |
| 10 | ~500 | ~60 |
| 50 | ~2500 | ~80 |
| 100 | ~5000 | ~100 |

Slot packing amortizes the homomorphic compute cost across all items in a single ciphertext. The dominant cost becomes the single `processEncrypted` call regardless of batch size.

## Dependencies

* Requires SEAL library support for batch encoding
* May need to increase `polyModulusDegree` in `seal-context.ts` from 8192 to 16384 for more slots
* `FHEEmotionClassifier` interface change is backward compatible (existing single-item `classify()` is unaffected)

## Files to Modify

* `src/lib/fhe/seal-context.ts` — possibly increase polyModulusDegree
* `src/lib/fhe/seal-service.ts` — add batch encode/decode methods
* `src/lib/fhe/fhe-service.ts` — add batch methods to RealFHEService
* `src/lib/fhe/mock/mock-fhe-service.ts` — mock batch methods
* `src/lib/fhe/types.ts` — BatchEncryptedData interface
* `src/lib/fhe/fhe-emotion-classifier.ts` — use batch methods in classifyBatch

issues.title: Pace Tracker Sub-agent: Parallel Workers AI Pacing Analysis for Session Agent
issues.description:
## Summary

Create a **Pace Tracker sub-agent** in the session-agent that runs Workers AI (`@cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct`) **in parallel** with the main Claude Opus inference loop. It analyzes the trainee's conversational rhythm and feeds pacing metadata into the session's `persistent_notes` field -- invisible to the trainee, but surfaced to supervisors across sessions.

## Problem

The session-agent processes every trainee turn with the same full pipeline: Claude Opus analyzes emotion, checks boundaries, and produces a reply. Therapeutic conversations have a natural rhythm -- rapid-fire questions, stuck reflection loops, topic avoidance -- but the agent has no awareness of pacing. It treats every turn in isolation.

The trainee gets excellent micro-responses but no macro-coaching signal. Supervisors reviewing sessions cannot see patterns of interaction (e.g., "the trainee spent 8 consecutive turns in reflection without moving to exploration").

## Solution

A lightweight Workers AI sub-agent that runs **alongside** (not before/after) the Claude Opus processing:

1. When a trainee turn arrives, the session-agent starts the Claude Opus pipeline *and* the Pace Tracker in parallel
2. Pace Tracker (Workers AI, 3B model, sub-second) analyzes the last 3-5 turns for rhythm patterns
3. It writes results to the session's durable state
4. The main Claude response finishes independently
5. The session-agent conditionally attaches pacing observations to `persistent_notes` -- no delay to the response

### Workers AI Pace Analysis Output

```json
{
  "stuck": false,
  "pattern": "reflection_loop|topic_avoidance|rapid_fire|normal",
  "consecutive_same_technique": 4,
  "suggestion": "5 consecutive empathetic reflections without progression -- consider shifting to an exploration technique",
  "conversation_flow": "the trainee's turns are getting shorter and more defensive"
}
```

## Why Workers AI / Why This Approach

* **Parallel execution** -- Workers AI is fast enough (sub-second for 3B) that it finishes before or alongside Claude Opus. No added latency.
* **Edge cost** -- Free tier covers 10k calls/day. At ~200 turns/session, that is 50 sessions/day free.
* **Cheap supervision metadata** -- Rather than burning Claude Opus tokens on meta-analysis, Workers AI produces coarse but sufficient pacing signals.
* **Novel use of Eve parallelism** -- Eve's sub-agent system runs independently alongside the main agent loop. This is the first sub-agent that does not *gate* the main agent but *enriches* it.
* **Persistent across sessions** -- The `persistent_notes` field in the output schema already exists for this purpose. Pacing patterns accumulate longitudinally.

## Implementation Plan

### Session 1 -- Pace Tracker Sub-agent + analyze_pace tool

**Files to create/modify:**

1. `agents/session-agent/agent/subagents/pace-tracker/agent.ts` -- New Eve sub-agent with Workers AI model
2. `agents/session-agent/agent/tools/analyze_pace.ts` -- Tool that receives recent turn history and returns pacing analysis
3. Modify `agents/session-agent/agent/tools/analyze_emotion.ts` -- Call the pace tracker in parallel
4. No new dependencies needed (workers-ai-provider already installed)

**The sub-agent definition:**

```ts
import { defineAgent } from "eve";
import { createWorkersAI } from "workers-ai-provider";

const workersai = createWorkersAI({
  accountId: process.env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID,
  apiKey: process.env.CLOUDFLARE_AI_API_KEY,
});

export default defineAgent({
  model: workersai("@cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct"),
  // ...
});
```

**The tool (**`analyze_pace`**):**

* Input: `{ recent_turns: Turn[], session_duration_minutes: number }`
* Output: structured pace analysis (stuck flag, pattern enum, suggestion text, conversation_flow summary)
* Calls the pace-tracker sub-agent, which uses Workers AI
* The parent agent merges the result into `persistent_notes` before writing the session record

### Session 2 -- Supervisor Dashboard Integration (if desired)

* Surface pacing history in the qa-agent's `generate_report` tool.
* Add a "pace profile" section to cohort summaries showing average technique-switching frequency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `analyze_pace` tool exists and typechecks
- [ ] Pace Tracker sub-agent registers with Workers AI model
- [ ] The main agent loop calls `analyze_pace` **in parallel** with Claude processing (no added latency)
- [ ] Pacing observations appear in `persistent_notes` when the pattern is non-trivial
- [ ] Works with graceful fallback when Workers AI credentials are missing (skips pace analysis)
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck` passes in session-agent
- [ ] Workers AI free tier model (`@cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct`) handles the prompt correctly

## Related

* Already deployed MCP server: `https://workers-ai-mcp.coburncd.workers.dev`
* Existing Workers AI tools: `analyze_emotion`, `check_clinical_boundary` (session-agent), `detect_emotional_patterns`, `score_session` (qa-agent)

issues.description:
Port the existing SQLite schema (29 Pydantic-backed tables) to PostgreSQL-compatible DDL and build a migration runner.

## Deliverables

1. `foresight_mcp/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql` — DDL for PostgreSQL with:
   * Proper PostgreSQL data types (e.g., `TEXT` instead of `VARCHAR`, `TIMESTAMPTZ`, `BOOLEAN`, `JSONB`)
   * `pgvector` extension for `embedding` columns (`vector(1536)`)
   * `SERIAL` / `IDENTITY` columns instead of `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`
   * `pg_tgrm` extension for full-text search indexes
   * All unique constraints, foreign keys, and indexes
   * Convert recursive CTEs to PostgreSQL-compatible syntax (already compatible)
2. `foresight_mcp/migrations/__init__.py` — migration runner
   * Track applied migrations in a `_migrations` metadata table
   * Apply unapplied migrations in order
   * Idempotent: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`
   * Rollback support via reverse DDL in separate `.sql` files

## Key Translation Points

| SQLite | PostgreSQL |
| -- | -- |
| `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` | `SERIAL PRIMARY KEY` or `BIGSERIAL` |
| `TEXT` / `VARCHAR` | `TEXT` / `VARCHAR(n)` |
| `REAL` | `DOUBLE PRECISION` / `REAL` |
| `BLOB` | `BYTEA` |
| `FOREIGN KEY ... deferrable` | `FOREIGN KEY ... DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` |
| `CREATE INDEX` | Same, plus `USING GIN` for JSONB |
| WAL mode | Not needed (PostgreSQL handles this natively) |
| `random()` | `random()` (same) |
| No extension | `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;` |

* `foresight_mcp/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql`

   * `async execute(sql: str, params: tuple = ()) -> None`

```python
class DatabaseBackend(ABC):

    async def connect(self) -> None: ...

    async def execute(self, sql: str, params: tuple = ()) -> None: ...
    @abstractmethod

    @abstractmethod
    async def fetch_one(self, sql: str, params: tuple = ()) -> dict | None: ...
    @abstractmethod
    async def executemany(self, sql: str, param_list: list[tuple]) -> None: ...
```

issues.title: Epic: Unified Cloud Memory Database for Foresight MCP
issues.description:
## Summary

Consolidate the 6+ per-agent SQLite databases into a single shared cloud database backing all Foresight MCP instances, plus an optional Redis companion for cross-agent caching and rate limiting.

## Motivation

Every agent machine currently runs its own Foresight MCP with an isolated SQLite database (`FORESIGHT_DB_PATH`). This means:

* **No shared memory** — Agent A's learnings are invisible to Agent B
* **No cross-agent coordination** — Rate limits, embedding caches, and hot data are duplicated per-instance
* **No zero-downtime deploys** — SQLite is process-bound; any restart drops the connection state
* **No horizontal scaling** — Each agent is coupled to its local file

Moving to a cloud PostgreSQL backend (Neon) solves all of these while preserving the existing query architecture.

## Design

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Agent 1  │  Agent 2  │  ...  │  Agent N    │
│  Foresight │  Foresight │       │  Foresight  │
│  MCP       │  MCP       │       │  MCP        │
└──────┬──────┴──────┬──────┘       └──────┬──────┘
       │             │                      │
       └─────────────┴──────┬───────────────┘
                            │
                ┌───────────▼───────────┐
                │   FORESIGHT_DB_URL     │  ← Neon PostgreSQL
                │  (shared cloud DB)     │
                │  + pgvector extension  │
                │  + Redis companion     │
                └───────────────────────┘
```

## Phases

| Phase | What | Depends On |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | DatabaseBackend protocol + SqliteBackend (abstraction layer) | — |
| 2 | PostgresBackend with asyncpg | Phase 1 |
| 3 | PostgreSQL-compatible DDL port + migration runner | Phase 2 |
| 4 | Adapt Hybrid Retriever + Graph Store for backend-agnostic queries | Phase 1 |
| 5 | Wire FORESIGHT_DB_URL configuration → backend factory | Phase 1-4 |
| 6 | Redis companion (cross-agent cache + rate limit coordination) | Phase 5 |
| 7 | Multi-agent deployment verification + Neon provisioning | Phase 5-6 |

## Key File Map

| Current (SQLite) | Target (Backend Protocol) |
| -- | -- |
| `connection_pool.py` → 5 ops (connect, execute, fetch, fetch_one, close) | `backend/base.py` — `DatabaseBackend` ABC |
| Same 5 ops | `backend/sqlite_backend.py` — wraps ConnectionPool |
| Same 5 ops + pool management | `backend/postgres_backend.py` — wraps asyncpg |
| `schema.py` (29 models) | `migrations/` — PostgreSQL DDL |
| `hybrid_retriever.py` | Backend-agnostic via `DatabaseBackend` |
| `graph_store.py` (recursive CTEs) | Backend-agnostic (CTEs work in both) |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All existing Foresight MCP tests pass with SqliteBackend (regression)
- [ ] All same tests pass with PostgresBackend against local Docker PostgreSQL
- [ ] Two agent instances can read/write the same Neon database concurrently

issues.title: Add clinical/safety/privacy-sensitive gating to memory maintenance
issues.description:
## Background

[PIX-3952](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3952/build-hands-off-memory-maintenance-jobs) implemented background memory maintenance (consolidation, contradiction detection, stale archival, synthesis) with automatic low-risk changes and admin-visible contradictions. A guardrail from that issue was deferred:

> *"Clinical/safety/privacy-sensitive memories require stricter gates."*

## Objective

Add a mechanism to tag or infer which memories contain clinical, safety-sensitive, or PHI content, and gate maintenance operations on those memories:

* Skip auto-consolidation of clinical/sensitive memories — flag them for human review instead.
* Never auto-archive sensitive memories, regardless of staleness.
* Add a `sensitive_only` mode or filter to `MaintenanceConfig` so operators can explicitly target or exclude sensitive memories.
* Log maintenance actions near sensitive memories with additional detail.

## Acceptance Criteria

* A storage-level or content-level signal identifies potentially sensitive memories (e.g., a `is_sensitive` column, keyword/phrase detection, or category tag).
* Maintenance modes (`consolidate`, `archive_stale`) respect the sensitive flag — low-risk automatic changes do not apply.
* Contradiction detection on sensitive memories is always flagged for admin review (already the default, but explicitly enforced).
* Tests verify sensitive memories are preserved during auto-consolidation and stale archival.
* Tenant isolation is maintained (sensitive flag is per-tenant).

issues.title: Refine automatic capture with add-only extraction and dedupe
issues.description:
## Objective

Improve automatic memory creation while preserving the hands-off model: capture useful facts, decisions, patterns, and entities without asking users to manage memory manually.

## Inspirations

* Mem0 single-pass ADD-only extraction to avoid complex update/delete loops.
* ByteRover session learning categories: patterns, preferences, entities, decisions, skills.
* opencode-mem idle capture and skip logic for non-technical conversations.

## Proposed Work

* Review current transcript/session capture pipeline.
* Add or refine extraction categories for coding-agent work: decisions, reusable patterns, entities/files, user preferences, successful tool recipes.
* Prefer append/add plus relationship metadata over destructive in-place mutation.
* Add deterministic dedupe/merge checks against recent memories before storing.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Short/trivial sessions are skipped automatically.
* Useful technical sessions produce compact categorized memories.
* Duplicate memories are skipped or linked rather than repeatedly injected.
* Decisions can remain immutable/auditable where appropriate.
* Tests cover skip, create, dedupe, and relationship/link behavior.

## Verification

* Confirm generated memories are concise enough to improve future payloads.

issues.title: Create evaluation harness for payload size and retrieval quality
issues.description:
## Objective

Make the sprint measurable. Track whether Foresight actually reduces context payload size and maintains/improves retrieval quality.

## Inspirations

* Mem0 publishes retrieval benchmarks and token-efficiency claims.
* ByteRover documents latency tiers and query behavior.
* Foresight already has evaluation concepts in memory-related code.

## Metrics to Capture

* Formatted injection payload size before/after budgeted lanes.
* Top-k retrieval precision on representative coding-agent queries.
* Recall for project decisions, pending items, and user preferences.
* Latency by retrieval path: cache/direct/hybrid.
* Rate of empty, stale, duplicate, or irrelevant memory injections.
* Safety/privacy checks for sensitive memory leakage.

## Acceptance Criteria

* A small reproducible fixture suite exists for memory retrieval and injection payloads.
* Harness reports payload size, latency, and quality metrics.
* Sprint changes include before/after comparison data.
* Safety checks include PII/secret leakage scanning in injected output.
* CI or local verification command is documented.

## Verification
