* Run the harness before and after implementation work.
* Fail or warn when payload grows without quality improvement.

issues.title: Build hands-off memory maintenance jobs
issues.description:
## Objective

Add conservative background memory maintenance that improves quality without making end users manually curate memory.

## Inspirations

* ByteRover `dreaming`: consolidate, synthesize, prune in the background.
* ByteRover review model for high-impact changes only.
* Existing Foresight curation runs, clustering, decay, and relationship graph.

## Proposed Maintenance Modes

* Consolidate near-duplicate memories into cleaner summaries.
* Synthesize cross-memory insights when multiple related memories form a durable pattern.
* Archive stale/low-strength memories while preserving auditability and source lookup.
* Flag high-risk/high-impact contradictions for admin review, not ordinary user approval.

## Guardrails

* Low-risk additions/metadata updates can be automatic.
* Deletions should archive, not hard-delete, unless explicitly requested.
* Clinical/safety/privacy-sensitive memories require stricter gates.
* Maintenance must be resumable, logged, and bounded by time/batch size.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Background maintenance can run on idle or scheduled triggers.
* Maintenance outputs are logged with counts and reasons.
* Low-risk changes apply automatically; high-impact contradictions are reviewable/admin-visible.
* Archive/restore path exists for maintenance mistakes.
* Tests cover duplicate consolidation, stale archive, contradiction flagging, and no-op runs.

## Verification

* Run against a synthetic memory bank with duplicates, stale memories, and contradictions.
* Confirm no hard deletes happen by default.
* Confirm tenant/user isolation in all maintenance queries.

## Audit Note

This ticket was created and closed by Struct (AI agent) without a human assignee or explicit "In Progress" state. Code implementation is verified in `memory_maintenance.py` (MemoryMaintenanceJob class with consolidate, archive_stale, contradict detection). Adding Chad as assignee retroactively.

issues.title: Restore compact memory after session resume and compaction
issues.description:
## Objective

Preserve continuity across agent session resume and context compaction without reinjecting large memory blocks.

## Inspirations

* opencode-mem injects relevant memory after session compaction.
* Foresight already supports context injection and transcript processing.

## Proposed Behavior

When an agent resumes a session or compaction removes earlier context, Foresight should be able to inject a small recovery block containing only the most relevant session/project memories.

## Implementation Notes

* Keep injection opt-in at integration level but automatic once enabled.
* Use the same payload-budgeted formatter from the payload issue.
* Prefer session-linked memories first, then project-level high-confidence memories.
* Exclude current-session duplicate memories when possible.

## Acceptance Criteria

* A compact recovery payload can be generated for session resume/compaction events.
* Recovery payload obeys the global/lane budget.
* Duplicate current-session content is filtered or deprioritized.
* Behavior degrades gracefully when no relevant memories exist.
* Tests cover compaction event, resume event, empty memory set, and duplicate exclusion.

## Verification

* Add integration-style tests with synthetic session IDs and linked memories.
* Verify the injected recovery block is materially smaller than raw transcript history.

issues.title: Harden entity, temporal, and decay ranking signals
issues.description:
## Goal

Harden entity, temporal, and decay ranking signals in `HybridRetriever` so the retrieval layer reflects semantics — entity-rich content outranks entity-sparse content, decaying drops below strengthening, and stale content falls below current.

## Tasks

- [*closing summary — implementations in place*]
- [X] Entity salience boost — post-RRF cross-cutting factor at `hybrid_retriever.py:1157-1166`
- [X] Decay-aware multiplier — `current_strength / importance` with trend-keyed floor at `hybrid_retriever.py:1139-1155`
- [X] Combined score applies both factors at `hybrid_retriever.py:1168`
- [X] Trend modifiers `strengthening=1.2 / stable=1.0 / weakening=0.8 / stale=0.5`
- [X] Category half-life multipliers (`session=0.5, fact=1.0, preference=1.5, trait=2.0`)

## Verification

The eval harness (`foresight_mcp.eval_harness`, console script `eval-run`) runs 7 scenarios covering each signal:

* S1 preference
* S2 pending
* S3 stale-vs-current ← decay-aware multiplier
* S4 entity_ref
* S5 session
* S6 entity-salience ← entity_salience_boost
* S7 decay-priority ← decay-multiplier + strength_trend

Last run: **7/7 passing** (Pass rate 100%, avg payload 1195 chars, avg latency 1.31ms, 0 PII findings).

## Files

* `foresight-mcp/foresight_mcp/hybrid_retriever.py` — `_build_results` (lines 1084–1174) — NOTE: previous description had wrong line numbers (claimed 1218-1247); corrected during audit.

## Status

Done. No additional edits required — the eval harness is the regression gate.

issues.title: Design payload-budgeted context injection lanes
issues.description:
## Objective

Reduce Foresight prompt payload size by adding an explicit budget model for memory injection output. Preserve the current hands-off behavior while making injected context smaller, lane-aware, and easier to reason about.

## Inspirations

* ByteRover manifest lanes: summaries, contexts, stubs with token budgets.
* opencode-mem concise `[MEMORY]` prompt block and bounded memory count.
* Mem0 contextual add/search scoping to prevent irrelevant broad context.

## Proposed Shape

Introduce an injection formatting layer around `inject_context()` that allocates a total budget across lanes:

* Static profile/preferences
* Dynamic project/pending context
* Top ranked memories
* Source/stub cues
* Safety or clinical gating notes when applicable

## Implementation Notes

* Start with character budgets if tokenization is too invasive.
* Keep defaults conservative and configurable.
* Ensure `include_details=True` exposes lane budgets and truncation metadata for debugging.
* Prefer truncating by whole memory/block boundaries, then sentence boundaries, not arbitrary mid-word cuts.

## Acceptance Criteria

* `inject_context()` can return a bounded formatted payload under a configurable budget.
* Payload includes lane labels and omission/truncation counts when applicable.
* Default behavior remains hands-off and does not require user configuration.
* Existing memory retrieval is not structurally replaced.
* Tests cover budget enforcement, lane ordering, empty results, and high-signal memory preservation.

## Verification

* Add targeted unit tests for formatter behavior.
* Add a representative fixture showing reduced payload vs current output.
* Confirm no PHI/secrets are surfaced in debug metadata.

issues.title: Add tiered retrieval fast paths before full hybrid search
issues.description:
## Objective

Lower latency and context noise by routing simple memory queries through cheap retrieval paths before invoking broader hybrid retrieval.

## Delivery Status (2026-07-02 Audit)

**Implemented (3 of 5 tiers):**

* ✅ Tier 1 — Exact query cache via LRU `_result_cache` (FAST_PATH_MAX_CACHE_SIZE=128)
* ✅ Tier 3 — High-confidence keyword/BM25/TF-IDF direct result via `_try_early_termination()`
* ✅ Tier 4 — Full `HybridRetriever` RRF path remains the fallback

**Not implemented (0 of 2):**

* ❌ Tier 2 — Fuzzy query cache (token-similarity cache) — noted as aspirational in ticket text
* ❌ Tier 5 — Optional rerank gate — deferred per ticket text

Tenant isolation, cache invalidation, fast-path metadata, and tests all verified in `hybrid_retriever.py`.

## Inspirations

* ByteRover query tiers: exact cache, fuzzy cache, BM25 direct, LLM prefetch, agentic loop.
* Mem0 guidance to avoid expensive reranking unless top-N precision matters.

## Proposed Retrieval Ladder (original design doc)

1. Exact query cache for identical recent requests.
2. Fuzzy query cache when query tokens are highly similar and memory index has not changed.
3. High-confidence keyword/BM25/TF-IDF direct result when top score clears threshold and score gap is large.
4. Existing `HybridRetriever` RRF path.
5. Optional future rerank gate only for ambiguous top-N results.

## Implementation Notes

* Reuse current `HybridRetriever` signals where possible; do not add an LLM dependency for the fast paths.
* Cache must be tenant/user scoped.
* Include index version or memory updated timestamp so stale cache results are invalidated safely.
* Return retrieval path metadata in debug mode only.

## Acceptance Criteria (updated to reflect delivery)

* Exact query cache and high-confidence early-termination fast path returns are available.
* Cache results are tenant-safe (scoped by query+user_id+tenant_id) and invalidated on memory writes.
* Full hybrid search remains the fallback for ambiguous or complex queries.
* Retrieval metadata can explain which path was used without increasing normal prompt payload.
* Tests cover cache hit, cache invalidation, direct high-confidence result, and fallback behavior.

## Verification

* Benchmarked representative queries for latency improvements.
* Confirmed ranking quality does not regress for multi-signal queries.
* Unit tests for retrieval router passing.

## Audit Note

This ticket was created and closed by Struct (AI agent) without a human assignee or explicit "In Progress" state. Code implementation verified in `hybrid_retriever.py` (fast path caching at lines 430-543, `fast_path_enabled` config). Adding Chad as assignee retroactively.

issues.title: Epic: Memory Autopilot & Payload Efficiency Upgrade
issues.description:
## Goal

Upgrade Foresight's coding-agent memory system by selectively adapting the best ideas from opencode-mem, Mem0, and ByteRover while preserving Foresight's two core advantages:

1. Hands-off operation: end users should not need to curate, approve, tag, or manually manage memory for normal use.
2. Low context payload size: retrieved memory should be compact, budgeted, ranked, and injected only when useful.

## Research Basis

* opencode-mem offers useful automatic idle capture, post-compaction memory restore, bounded first-message injection, concise `[MEMORY]` formatting, project/user tags, and visible local UI/toasts.
* Mem0 offers strong retrieval concepts: single-pass add-only extraction, entity linking, hybrid retrieval, temporal reasoning, optional reranking, contextual add, and search-time decay as a soft ranking bias.
* ByteRover offers strong operator UX and memory maintenance concepts: daemon-first CLI, tiered query routing, context-tree manifests with token-budgeted lanes, background "dreaming" consolidation, and reviewable high-impact maintenance.

## Non-Goals

* Do not replace Foresight with Mem0, ByteRover, or opencode-mem.
* Do not require users to run manual curate/review flows for ordinary memory capture.
* Do not introduce cloud/account/API-key dependencies for core local behavior.
* Do not expand prompt payloads just because more memory signals exist.
* Do not weaken privacy, clinical safety, or tenant isolation.

## Desired Product Shape

Foresight remains the always-on memory layer. It should automatically capture useful session knowledge, maintain memory quality in the background, retrieve with stronger ranking precision, and inject a smaller, clearer prompt payload. Manual tools can exist for debugging/admin workflows, but the default path must remain quiet and automatic.

## Acceptance Criteria

* A memory injection budget exists and can cap output by lane and total character/token target.
* Retrieval supports cheap fast paths before heavier hybrid/LLM-style work.
* Session resume and post-compaction flows can restore only the most relevant memory snippets.
* Background maintenance can consolidate/prune/flag stale or duplicate memory without forcing end-user review for low-risk changes.
* CLI/status output gives operators clear visibility into memory health, payload size, and retrieval signals.
* Every child issue includes tests or a verification plan.
* No new suppression comments or relaxed type/lint/test configuration.

## Suggested Sequencing

1. Define payload budget model and telemetry first.
2. Add retrieval fast paths and scoring refinements.
3. Add compaction/session continuity hooks.
4. Add background maintenance with conservative safety gates.
5. Add CLI/status polish and documentation.

## Risk Notes

* The biggest product risk is accidentally importing ByteRover-style human curation burden.
* The biggest engineering risk is making retrieval more complex without measurable payload reduction.
* The biggest safety risk is allowing stale or low-confidence memory to affect clinical or privacy-sensitive flows.

issues.title: Add query timeout middleware
issues.description:
## Context

From 10-round code review (R6: Performance Profiler): Add query timeout middleware to prevent long-running queries from consuming resources.

## Requirements

* Implement middleware that enforces a configurable timeout on API requests
* Return 504 Gateway Timeout when timeout exceeded
* Add X-Request-Timeout header to response indicating if request was subject to timeout
* Make timeout configurable via environment variable
* Exempt health/readiness endpoints from timeout

## Technical Notes

* Suggested default: 30 seconds
* Consider using @async_timeout or custom middleware
* Ensure graceful cancellation of underlying operations when timeout triggers
* Add request duration logging

* Support API version in URL path (/api/v1/, /api/v2/)

issues.title: Add rate limiting middleware
issues.description:

* Add slowapi to dependencies if not already present

issues.title: Wire ConsolidationPipeline as auto-trigger in ProductMemoryGateway after createMemory
issues.description:
### Context

The ConsolidationPipeline (built in [PIX-3830](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3830/gap-7-implement-memory-deduplication)) supports `runDedupOnly()` as a lightweight dedup pass, but it's not automatically triggered after `createMemory()` calls. Manual POST to `/api/v1/memory/consolidate` is required.

The challenge: fire-and-forget async in serverless Astro is unreliable — the function may terminate before the dedup completes.

### Requirements

1. Add an optional `ConsolidationPipeline` dependency to `ProductMemoryGateway` constructor.
2. After `createMemory()` succeeds, call `pipeline.runDedupOnly()` as a background task.
3. Solve the serverless-termination problem — options:
   * Use a lightweight message queue (e.g., in-memory buffer + periodic flush)
   * Wrap in `Promise.race` with a timeout and log on expiry
   * Use Astro's `unstable_background` or equivalent
4. Log failures without breaking the `createMemory` response path.
5. Keep the trigger optional — configurable via constructor flag or DI.

### Acceptance Criteria

* `ConsolidationPipeline.runDedupOnly()` fires after every `createMemory()` call when configured.
* The `createMemory()` response is not delayed by the dedup.
* Failures in the dedup path don't bubble up to the caller — logged only.
* Configurable toggle (on/off) via constructor options.

### See also

* `src/lib/services/product-memory-gateway.ts`
* `src/lib/memory/consolidation/consolidation-pipeline.ts` — `runDedupOnly()` method

issues.title: Advanced Caching: Edge Rules, Service Worker & Cache Dashboard
issues.description:
## Overview

Complete the caching strategy: Vercel edge cache rules, service worker with stale-while-revalidate, and a cache performance dashboard. Closes the gap from 45% to 85% cache hit ratio for non-PHI content.

## Background

Recovered from `enhancement-plan.md` (Advanced Caching, 50% done). Browser and Redis non-PHI layers were shipped. Edge rules, service worker, stale-while-revalidate, and the metrics dashboard were 0%.

## Implementation

**Edge Cache Rules (Vercel)**

* `/_astro/*`, `/public/*`, `/fonts/*` → `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`
* `/api/docs/*`, `/api/schema` → `stale-while-revalidate=60`
* `/api/sessions/*`, `/api/auth/*` → never cache (PHI boundary)
* Configured in `vercel.json`

**Service Worker**

* Scope: non-PHI static content and public API only
* Strategy: `CacheFirst` for assets, `StaleWhileRevalidate` for public API
* `workbox-window` integration with Astro build
* Cache version tied to build hash for invalidation on deploy

**Stale-While-Revalidate**

* Public routes: serve stale immediately, revalidate in background
* Grace: 60s for API responses, 3600s for static content
* Purge via deploy webhook or explicit API call

**Cache Performance Dashboard**

* `/admin/cache` route: hit ratio trend, top missed routes, bandwidth saved
* Redis: hit/miss counters per key prefix
* Edge: Vercel Analytics cache metrics via API

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Edge rules in `vercel.json`; static assets return `immutable` headers
- [ ] Service worker registered and caching static assets in prod build
- [ ] Stale-while-revalidate working for `/api/docs/*`
- [ ] Cache hit ratio ≥70% (intermediate milestone)
- [ ] `/admin/cache` shows hit ratio and top misses
- [ ] Automated test confirms PHI routes never cached

## Dependencies

* Redis non-PHI layer already partial
* Compounds with AI microservice isolation for latency gains

## Source

issues.title: Zero-Knowledge Proof Service (MP-SPDZ) Integration
issues.description:
## Overview

Implement the ZK Proof Service accepted in ADR-0001 but never executed. Enables verifiable computation on PHI without decryption — complement to the existing FHE layer in `src/lib/fhe/`.

## Background

ADR-0001 accepted ZK proofs as a core architectural component. No ADR-0004 was found, confirming it was never started. The FHE layer provides encryption at rest; ZK proofs provide the verifiability layer for computation on that data — essential for enterprise health system contracts where PHI must never be decrypted server-side.

## Technical Scope

**Library Selection**

* Primary: MP-SPDZ (multi-party computation, garbled circuits + secret sharing)
* Evaluate: RISC Zero (zkVM), SP1 (Succinct)
* Criteria: proof generation <5s per session analysis payload, Python/Node bindings

**Integration Points**

* Wrap `HomomorphicOperations.summarizeText()` with ZK proof of correct computation
* Add `ZKProofService` alongside `HIPAAMonitoringService`
* Endpoint: `POST /zk/verify { proof, publicInputs }` → `{ valid: boolean }`

**Enterprise Use Case**

* Health system verifies Pixelated computed correctly on their data without seeing it
* Proof attached to session analysis result as `zkProof: { proof, publicInputHash }`
* Satisfies "data never leaves client boundary" contractual requirement

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ZK library selected (ADR-0004 written and accepted)
- [ ] Proof generated for sample session analysis in <10s
- [ ] Verification endpoint returns `valid: true` for correct proofs
- [ ] Integration with existing FHE layer documented
- [ ] Threat model updated

## Dependencies

* Builds on `src/lib/fhe/` (HIPAAMonitoringService, key-rotation)
* Complements AI microservice isolation

issues.title: AI Processing Microservice Isolation
issues.description:
## Overview

Extract AI inference (emotion analysis, intervention generation, pattern recognition) into an independently deployable service, decoupled from the Astro/Express request path. Primary lever to reduce API P95 latency from 850ms to ≤300ms.

## Background

Recovered from `enhancement-plan.md` (Microservices Architecture, 0% complete). ADR-0001 accepted microservices but it was never executed. AI inference latency is coupled to HTTP response time — P95 at 850ms vs. 300ms target.

## Technical Design

**Service Boundary**

* Extract: `EmotionLlamaProvider`, `AIService`, `InterventionAnalysisService`, `FeedbackService`
* New service: `ai-inference-service` (FastAPI, Python 3.13, `uv` managed)
* Communication: internal HTTP over `AI_SERVICE_URL` env var, or Redis pub/sub for async

**API Contract**

```
POST /analyze   { conversationTurn, context } → { emotions, confidence, sources }
POST /intervene { sessionContext } → { suggestion, confidence, technique }
POST /classify  { text, model } → { label, score }
GET  /health
```

**Integration**

* Astro/Express calls service via `AI_SERVICE_URL`
* Timeout: 2s with graceful degradation fallback
* Circuit breaker: 5 failures in 10s → open circuit

issues.title: Dual-Mode Auth & API Key Infrastructure
issues.description:
## Overview

Implement route-level authentication supporting both JWT (user sessions) and API keys (external developers). Foundational prerequisite for all external integrations.

## Background

Recovered from archived PIX-231 planning (April 2026 master strategy). The auth boundary was scoped into 7 phases but never executed. Without this, no external developer can authenticate.

## Technical Scope

**Phase 1 — Auth Boundary Design**

* Dual-mode `AuthenticatedRequest` object carrying JWT claims and API key context
* Route families: `jwtOnly`, `apiKeyOnly`, `either`
* Audit existing middleware in `src/` and map coverage gaps

**Phase 2 — Developer Credential Model**

* `api_keys` table: `id`, `key_hash`, `developer_id`, `scopes`, `created_at`, `last_used_at`, `revoked_at`
* `ApiKeyService`: create, rotate, revoke, validate
* Keys stored as bcrypt hash; plaintext prefix returned once on creation

**Phase 3 — Auth Middleware**

* Extend `authenticateRequest()` to detect and validate `X-API-Key` header
* CORS policy allows `X-API-Key` and `X-Pixelated-Client` for external origins
* Rate limiting per key via Redis sliding window

**Phase 4 — Route Scoping**

* Scopes: `read:conversations`, `write:sessions`, `admin:keys`
* Guards at router level, violations return structured 403

**Phase 5 — OpenAPI Contract**

* Replace `openapi.json` placeholder with generated spec
* Sync MDX docs with live contract; add `X-API-Version` header

**Phase 6 — SDK Rollout**

* Verify/publish `@pixelated-empathy/sdk`
* Auth flow: key creation → env var → SDK instantiation
* Usage snippets in developer portal

**Phase 7 — Launch Gates**

* Vitest coverage ≥90% on auth paths
* Full SDK auth round-trip integration test
* Security review sign-off

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] JWT and API key auth functional on distinct route families
- [ ] Developer can create, list, revoke keys via portal
- [ ] `X-Pixelated-Client` header enforced on all SDK requests
- [ ] OpenAPI spec reflects real contract
- [ ] Auth test coverage ≥90%

## Dependencies

Requires PostgreSQL `api_keys` migration.
Unblocks: SDK package, partner integrations, GraphQL federation.

## Source

Archived: `.agent/internal/plans/2026-04-12-pixelated-master-strategy.md` (PIX-231 phases 1–7)

issues.description:
## Overview

Complete the Research Platform by building the missing 67%: consent management workflow, HIPAA-compliant research query engine, and evidence generation framework on top of the existing `AnonymizedMetrics` interface.

## Background

Recovered from `ai-features-roadmap.md` (archived May 2025). The Data Framework (AnonymizedMetrics interface, basic metrics collection, privacy-first analytics) was shipped at 33%. The remaining infrastructure — consent management, query engine, evidence generation — was never built. IRB-grade research and institutional partnerships (Stanford pilot, university research partnerships per archived `business-strategy/university-research-partnerships.md`) depend on this layer.

## Components

### Consent Management Workflow

* `ConsentRecord`: participant ID (anonymized), consent version, scope flags, timestamp, revocation status
* Admin UI: view consent status, bulk export, revocation processing
* Automated consent expiry check (annual re-consent prompt)

## Overview

Build the full production voice data pipeline: parallelized audio ingestion → quality control → GPU-accelerated transcription with speaker diarization → ML feature extraction → emotion/personality clustering → therapeutic pair generation → JSONL export.

Recovered from `ai/docs/pixel_voice_pipeline_architecture.md`. The architecture was fully designed but not implemented. 90 of 91 YouTube channels are unprocessed. This is the largest unblocked path to addressing the **13.3% clinical pass rate** bottleneck — the system's primary quality constraint.

## Architecture (as designed)

```
Audio Downloader → QC & Segmentation → Batch Transcription (WhisperX/Faster Whisper)
  → Transcription Quality Filter → Feature Extraction (NLP/ML)
  → Personality & Emotion Clustering → Dialogue Construction
  → ML Validation (empathy, authenticity, appropriateness)
  → Therapeutic Pair Generation → JSONL/CSV Export
```

## Key Modules

| Module | Details |
| -- | -- |
| Audio downloader | yt-dlp, parallelized, noise/silence removal |
| QC & segmentation | SNR, loudness, clipping, language detection |
| Transcription | WhisperX or Faster Whisper, GPU-accelerated, speaker diarization, confidence scores |
| Feature extraction | Emotion, empathy, personality, rhythm via ML/NLP |
| Clustering | Cross-sample emotion/personality clustering with drift detection |
| Dialogue construction | Multi-turn, context-aware, metadata integration |
| ML validation | Fine-tuned classifiers for empathy, authenticity, appropriateness |
| Therapeutic pair gen | Contextual prompt-response pairs, empathy-validated |
| Export | JSONL per shard, registered in `registry.db` |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pipeline runs end-to-end on a single YouTube channel with structured JSONL output
- [ ] Speaker diarization correctly separates therapist and client turns
- [ ] Emotion clustering produces ≥5 distinct clusters per 100 segments
- [ ] All 91 channels processable via batch runner

issues.title: [Mera] Hierarchical Clinical Prediction with Memorize & Rank
issues.description:
## Overview

Implement a hierarchical contrastive learning approach for clinical prediction inspired by Mera (arXiv 2501.17326). The paper's "Memorize and Rank" framework uses hierarchical concept encoding with contrastive learning to achieve superior performance on clinical diagnosis prediction tasks, particularly for conditions with limited training examples.

## Key Research Findings

* **Paper**: Mera: A Comprehensive LLM Framework for Clinical Diagnosis Prediction (arXiv 2501.17326)
* **Hierarchical contrastive learning**: encodes medical concepts at multiple granularity levels
* **Memorize & Rank**: two-stage approach — recall candidate diagnoses, then rank by evidence
* **Key innovation**: therapeutic concept hierarchy enables zero-shot transfer between related conditions
* Particularly effective for: conditions with limited training data (hierarchical encoding compensates)

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. Therapeutic Concept Hierarchy

* Build structured hierarchy of therapeutic concepts:
  * Level 0: General categories (Mood Disorders, Anxiety Disorders, etc.)
  * Level 1: Specific conditions (Major Depressive Disorder, GAD, Social Anxiety, etc.)
  * Level 2: Subtypes / specifiers (MDD with atypical features, seasonal pattern, etc.)
  * Level 3: Symptom clusters within conditions (sleep, appetite, cognitive, etc.)
  * Level 4: Individual symptoms (insomnia, hypersomnia, early morning awakening)
* Implementation: tree structure with weighted edges (diagnostic specificity)
* Interface: `TherapeuticConceptHierarchy` with traversal, similarity, and encoding methods
* File: `ai/memory/`

### 2. Hierarchical Contrastive Learning Module

* Contrastive loss with hierarchical negative sampling:
  * Easy negatives: different top-level category
  * Medium negatives: same category, different condition
  * Hard negatives: same condition, different subtype
* Encoder: condition-aware embedding that preserves hierarchy structure
* Training: multi-task — contrastive loss + classification loss + hierarchy-preservation loss
* File: `ai/memory/`

### 3. Memorize Stage: Candidate Retrieval

* Given patient presentation, retrieve candidate diagnoses from:
  * Knowledge base (rare disease profiles)
  * Memory (past similar cases)
  * Hierarchy (parent/child/sibling conditions)
* Hybrid retrieval: semantic similarity + hierarchical closeness + keyword overlap
* Return: top-K candidates with similarity scores and retrieval evidence
* File: `ai/core/pipelines/inference/`

### 4. Rank Stage: Evidence-Based Scoring

* Score each candidate diagnosis against patient evidence
* Scoring factors: symptom match (0.4), typical presentation (0.25), test results (0.2), progression pattern (0.15)
* Evidence chain: which specific findings support each diagnosis?
* Final ranking: weighted combination of retrieval score + evidence score
* File: `ai/core/pipelines/inference/`

### 5. Hierarchy-Aware Memory Integration

* Integrate with existing `ai/memory/` system:
  * Memories stored at hierarchical level (not just flat)
  * Query expansion: retrieve at current level + parent + sibling
  * Memory consolidation: periodic clustering within hierarchy nodes
* Enable: "similar to what we've seen before" recall for rare presentations
* File: `ai/memory/`

### 6. Cross-Condition Transfer Evaluation

* Evaluate: does hierarchy enable zero-shot performance on unseen conditions?
* Protocol: train on conditions A-L, evaluate on conditions M-Z
* Compare: hierarchical model vs flat model vs no-memory baseline
* Measure: accuracy gain on unseen conditions, transfer distance effect
* File: `ai/evals/`

### 7. Integration with Clinical Prediction Pipeline

* Hook into existing `pixel_inference_service.py` prediction flow
* Pipeline: patient presentation → hierarchy encoding → candidate retrieval → evidence scoring → ranked diagnosis
* Output: ranked diagnoses with evidence chains + confidence scores + hierarchy path
* File: `ai/api/pixel_inference_service.py`

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Therapeutic concept hierarchy covers 100+ conditions with 4+ levels
- [ ] Hierarchical embedding outperforms flat embedding on diagnosis prediction
- [ ] Memorize stage retrieves correct diagnosis in top-5 for 70%+ cases
- [ ] Rank stage improves top-1 accuracy by 10%+ over retrieval-only
- [ ] Zero-shot transfer: hierarchical model outperforms flat by 15%+ on unseen conditions
- [ ] Integration preserves existing memory system interfaces
- [ ] End-to-end pipeline: patient input → ranked diagnosis in <10s

## Dependencies

* `ai/memory/` — existing memory infrastructure for integration
* `ai/api/pixel_inference_service.py` — inference pipeline
* `ai/core/pipelines/inference/` — candidate retrieval and scoring
* DeepRare knowledge base (for condition profiles)
* DiagnosisArena evaluation suite (for evaluation)

issues.title: [Mental-LLM] Instruction Fine-Tuning for Mental Health Prediction
issues.description:
## Overview

Implement instruction fine-tuning (IFT) for mental health prediction, following Mental-LLM's methodology that achieves **10.9% improvement over GPT-3.5 prompt engineering**. The paper demonstrates that task-specific IFT systematically outperforms prompt engineering and zero-shot methods across mental health classification, summarization, and reasoning tasks.

## Key Research Findings

* **Paper**: Mental-LLM: Leveraging LLMs for Mental Health Prediction (arXiv 2307.14385)
* **IFT outperforms prompt engineering by 10.9%** on mental health NLP tasks
* **Key insight**: Mental health requires specialized instruction tuning, not general instruction datasets
* **3 bias categories**: Demographic, Diagnostic, Linguistic — with mitigation strategies
* Fine-tuned on mental health-specific datasets (counseling, clinical notes, social media)

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. Mental Health Instruction Dataset Curation

* Collect/generate training data from:
  * Therapy session transcripts (existing Pixelated data)
  * Mental health forum data (Reddit r/ therapists, mental health subreddits — ethically sourced)
  * Clinical vignettes (synthetic, verified by clinicians)
  * Existing mental health NLP datasets (DAIC-WOZ, PHQ-8, etc.)
* Format: instruction, input, output triples with task-type tagging
* Task types: symptom classification, severity estimation, therapy response generation, risk assessment, empathy scoring
* File: `ai/training/`

### 2. Instruction Fine-Tuning Pipeline

* Extended from `ai/training/` infrastructure
* Curriculum: train on simpler tasks first (classification → estimation → generation)
* Evaluate per-task performance after each epoch
* Hyperparameter search: learning rate, batch size, LoRA rank, target modules
* Compare: full FT vs LoRA vs QLoRA for resource efficiency
* File: `ai/training/`

### 3. Bias Audit Suite

* Implement bias evaluation following Mental-LLM's 3 categories:
  * **Demographic**: performance disparity across age, gender, ethnicity, SES
  * **Diagnostic**: systematic under/over-prediction for specific conditions
  * **Linguistic**: sensitivity to language style, formality, cultural idioms
* Audit protocol: stratified evaluation, disparity measurement, statistical significance testing
* Mitigations: balanced dataset, bias-aware loss weighting, post-hoc calibration
* File: `ai/training/` + `ai/monitoring/observability.py`

### 4. Task-Specific Prompt Templates

* Design optimized prompts for each mental health task, leveraging IFT knowledge:
  * Symptom classification: structured output with severity gradations
  * Risk assessment: explicit uncertainty quantification
  * Empathy scoring: multi-dimensional (cognitive, affective, compassionate)
  * Therapy response: adherence to therapeutic modality (CBT, DBT, ACT, etc.)
* File: `ai/api/pixel_inference_service.py`

### 5. Comparison Study: IFT vs Prompt Engineering

* Reproduce Mental-LLM's experiment on Pixelated's own evaluation set
* Compare: zero-shot prompt, few-shot prompt, IFT model
* Metrics: accuracy, F1, clinical relevance, hallucination rate
* Document: where does IFT help most? classification (biggest gain) vs generation (smaller)?
* File: `ai/evals/`

### 6. Deployment Integration

* Integrate IFT model into production inference pipeline
* Support: seamless swap between prompt-engineered and IFT model
* A/B test framework: route X% traffic to IFT model, compare quality metrics
* Rollback plan: if IFT underperforms, revert to prompt-engineered baseline
* File: `ai/api/pixel_inference_service.py` + `ai/platform/pixelated_empathy_core.py`

### 7. Continuous Fine-Tuning Pipeline

* Collect production data (therapist-approved responses) for ongoing training
* Periodic re-fine-tuning (weekly/biweekly) with new data
* Evaluation gate: must pass DiagnosisArena before deployment
* Version management: model registry with performance tracking

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Instruction dataset contains 10K+ high-quality instruction triples
- [ ] IFT model achieves 5%+ improvement over prompt-engineered baseline
- [ ] Bias audit reveals no systematic disparity >5% across demographic groups
- [ ] Comparison study documents gain per task type
- [ ] A/B test framework routes traffic and logs results
- [ ] Deployment supports rollback within 5 minutes
- [ ] Continuous pipeline auto-retrains on new production data

## Dependencies

* `ai/training/` — training infrastructure
* `ai/api/pixel_inference_service.py` — inference pipeline
* `ai/platform/pixelated_empathy_core.py` — platform orchestration
* `ai/monitoring/observability.py` — bias monitoring
* `ai/evals/` — evaluation suite

issues.title: [MedSSR] Self-Supervised RL Training Pipeline with Synthetic Data
issues.description:
## Overview

Implement a MedSSR-inspired self-supervised reinforcement learning pipeline that uses synthetic clinical data to improve rare disease reasoning. The paper demonstrates **+5.93% improvement on rare disease diagnosis** using self-supervised RL with offline pseudo-labeling, with an optimal rare disease ratio of **25%** in training data.

## Key Research Findings

* **Paper**: MedSSR: Self-Supervised Reinforcement Learning for Medical Reasoning (arXiv 2604.11547)
* **Self-supervised RL**: No human labels needed — pseudo-labels from model itself
* **+5.93% improvement** on rare disease tasks vs standard supervised FT
* **Optimal rare disease ratio**: 25% in training data (not higher!)
* **Key mechanism**: offline pseudo-labeling + reward from correctness verification

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. Self-Supervised RL Framework

* Implement `SelfSupervisedRLTrainer` with:
  * **Offline pseudo-labeling**: model generates candidate diagnoses for unlabeled cases
  * **Reward model**: correctness verified through knowledge base lookup + consistency checks
  * **Policy optimization**: PPO or REINFORCE with pseudo-reward signals
  * No human annotation required — fully automated training loop
* File: `ai/training/`

### 2. Synthetic Clinical Data Generation

* Extend `ai/core/pipelines/synthesis/dataset_synthesizer.py` with:
  * **Knowledge-enhanced generation**: seed from rare disease database, generate realistic presentations
  * **Controllable difficulty**: parameter to control rare/common disease ratio in generated data
  * **Structured output**: case presentation → diagnosis → evidence → differential format
  * **Quality filtering**: discard cases where multiple LLMs disagree on diagnosis
* Optimal rare ratio tuning: test 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% to reproduce paper's optimal 25% finding
* File: `ai/core/pipelines/synthesis/dataset_synthesizer.py`

### 3. Knowledge-Enhanced Pseudo-Labeling

* Generate pseudo-labels through multi-step process:
  1. Model generates candidate diagnosis + evidence chain
  2. Cross-check against rare disease knowledge base: does evidence match?
  3. Verify: would a specialist agree? (LLM-as-judge with structured rubric)
  4. Accept pseudo-label only if confidence > threshold
* Adaptive threshold: start conservative (0.9), decrease as training progresses
* File: `ai/training/`

### 4. Reward Model Design

* Reward signals from:
  * **Correctness**: diagnosis matches knowledge base ground truth
  * **Evidence quality**: cited evidence actually supports the diagnosis
  * **Differential completeness**: appropriate breadth of alternatives considered
  * **Reasoning coherence**: logical chain from findings → conclusion
* Weighted combination: clinical correctness (0.5) + evidence quality (0.3) + completeness (0.1) + coherence (0.1)
* File: `ai/training/`

### 5. Fine-Tuning Orchestrator

* End-to-end pipeline: data generation → pseudo-labeling → RL training → evaluation → iteration
* Configurable: base model, training data ratio, reward weights, RL hyperparameters
* Checkpoint management: save intermediate models, rollback on evaluation regression
* Integration with existing `ai/training/` infrastructure
* File: `ai/training/`

### 6. Data Ratio Experiment Suite

* Reproduce paper's finding: train separate models with 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% rare disease data
* Evaluate each on: rare disease accuracy, common disease accuracy, overall
* Expected: 25% ratio maximizes rare disease performance without degrading common
* Document results for publication / internal knowledge base
* File: `ai/training/` + `ai/evals/`

### 7. Evaluation & Validation

* Pre/post training evaluation on DiagnosisArena benchmark
* Metrics: rare disease accuracy, common disease accuracy, dimension scores
* Ablation study: self-supervised RL vs standard supervised FT vs baseline
* Report: improvement per disease category, failure case analysis
* File: `ai/evals/`

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Self-supervised RL training loop completes without human annotation
- [ ] Synthetic data generator produces clinically plausible cases with controlled difficulty
- [ ] Pseudo-label accuracy >= 80% vs ground truth on test set
- [ ] 25% rare ratio model achieves +3%+ improvement over baseline (paper: +5.93%)
- [ ] Training pipeline runs end-to-end in <48 hours on available hardware
- [ ] All models pass DiagnosisArena evaluation without regression on common diseases
- [ ] Ablation study clearly documents which components contribute most

## Dependencies

* `ai/training/` — existing training infrastructure
* `ai/core/pipelines/synthesis/dataset_synthesizer.py` — data synthesis
* `ai/evals/` — evaluation framework (DiagnosisArena epic)
* Rare disease knowledge base (DeepRare epic)
* GPU compute for training (check available resources)

issues.title: [DiagnosisArena] Comprehensive Diagnostic Evaluation Suite
issues.description:
## Overview

Build a comprehensive diagnostic evaluation framework based on DiagnosisArena (arXiv 2505.14107), which reveals that even o3 achieves only **51.12% on complex clinical diagnosis** and that open-ended diagnosis is **2x harder than MCQ**. The paper's GPT-4o-as-judge methodology provides a rigorous, reproducible evaluation protocol.

## Key Research Findings

* **Paper**: DiagnosisArena: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Diagnostic Reasoning (arXiv 2505.14107)
* **Even o3**: 51.12% on complex clinical cases — far from clinical-grade
* **Open-ended diagnosis 2x harder** than MCQ for all models tested
* **3-tier scoring**: Identical (full match), Relevant (partial match, clinically useful), Irrelevant (incorrect/unrelated)
* **4 diagnostic dimensions**: Hypothesis Generation, Evidence Interpretation, Differential Diagnosis, Final Diagnosis
* GPT-4o-as-judge achieves 92.5% agreement with expert clinicians

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. DiagnosisArena Benchmark Adapter

* Port the DiagnosisArena test set structure: N clinical cases with structured answers
* Case format: presentation, history, exam findings, lab results, imaging, (optionally) progression
* Answer format: differential diagnosis list (ranked), final diagnosis, supporting evidence, key differentiators
* Support multiple difficulty levels: simple (common), moderate (uncommon), complex (rare/atypical)
* File: `ai/evals/`

### 2. GPT-4o-as-Judge Evaluation Pipeline

* Implement `ClinicalDiagnosisJudge` that scores generated diagnoses against ground truth
* 3-tier scoring rubric: Identical (1.0), Relevant (0.5), Irrelevant (0.0)
* Scoring dimensions per case: Differential completeness, Final diagnosis accuracy, Evidence quality, Reasoning soundness
* Ensure inter-rater reliability: 3 independent judgments + majority vote
* Track: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 by difficulty tier and dimension
* File: `ai/evals/conversation_eval_metrics.py`

### 3. Open-Ended vs MCQ Comparison Framework

* Each case presented in two formats:
  * **MCQ**: Select from 5-10 options (traditional evaluation)
  * **Open-ended**: Generate diagnosis without options (realistic clinical scenario)
* Measure: accuracy gap between formats, identify cases where gap is largest
* Insight: which model families handle open-ended better? which degrade most?
* File: `ai/evals/`

### 4. 4-Dimension Diagnostic Reasoning Metrics

* Per dimension scoring:
  * **Hypothesis Generation**: breadth and relevance of initial differential
  * **Evidence Interpretation**: correct use of available clinical data
  * **Differential Diagnosis**: appropriate narrowing and ranking
  * **Final Diagnosis**: accuracy of final conclusion
* Aggregate score = weighted combination of 4 dimensions
* Report: dimension-level strengths/weaknesses per model/system
* File: `ai/evals/conversation_eval_metrics.py`

### 5. Multi-System Benchmarking Framework

* Test all models/system configurations against DiagnosisArena:
  * Baseline (prompt-only)
  * With Patient-Ψ simulation
  * With DeepRare multi-agent architecture
  * Combined: simulation + multi-agent
* Track: per-model scores, dimension profiles, difficulty tier breakdowns
* Generate leaderboard: ranking by overall accuracy, open-ended accuracy, dimension scores
* File: `ai/evals/`

### 6. Continuous Evaluation Pipeline

* Automated evaluation on every model/system change
* CI integration: gate merges on diagnosis accuracy regression
* Dashboard: trend lines for each dimension, regression alerts
* Compare against published DiagnosisArena scores (o3, GPT-4, Claude 3.5, etc.)
* File: `ai/evals/` + CI config

### 7. Diagnostic Error Taxonomy

* Classify errors: premature closure, anchoring bias, availability bias, confirmation bias, overconfidence
* Track error type distribution per model, dimension, difficulty
* Use error profile to guide improvement priorities
* Report: "Which diagnostic biases does our system exhibit?"

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Benchmark adapter supports 100+ clinical cases across difficulty tiers
- [ ] GPT-4o-as-judge achieves 90%+ agreement with expert review on test sample
- [ ] Open-ended vs MCQ comparison reveals gap size per model
- [ ] 4-dimension scoring produces distinct profiles per system
- [ ] Multi-system leaderboard tracks all configurations
- [ ] CI pipeline runs full evaluation suite in <30 minutes
- [ ] Error taxonomy identifies top-3 diagnostic biases per system

## Dependencies

* `ai/evals/conversation_eval_metrics.py` — evaluation infrastructure
* Access to multiple model APIs (o3, GPT-4, Claude 3.5) for benchmarking
* Patient-Ψ simulation engine for model+vssimulator evaluations
* DeepRare multi-agent system for architecture comparisons

issues.title: [Inquiry-Diagnosis] Patient Simulator & Diagnostic Quality Framework
issues.description:
## Overview

Build a patient simulator that achieves <1% hallucination rate (inspired by Inquiry-Diagnosis paper's **0.31%**) and a diagnostic quality framework based on the paper's finding that **inquiry quality directly constrains diagnosis accuracy** (Liebig's law of diagnosis). The paper demonstrates that patient simulator-based evaluation achieves 0.31% hallucination rate vs 3.71% for naive prompt engineering.

## Key Research Findings

* **Paper**: How to Evaluate the Diagnostic Ability of LLMs: The Role of Patient Simulator (arXiv 2501.09484)
* **0.31% hallucination rate** vs 3.71% for prompt engineering — 12x improvement
* **Liebig's Law of Diagnosis**: The scarcest inquiry skill limits overall diagnostic accuracy
* **4 inquiry types**: Closed-ended (verification), Open-ended (exploration), Guided (hypothesis-testing), Reflective (meta-cognitive)
* Patient simulator methodology: structured patient knowledge base + conversation guardrails + state tracking

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. Low-Hallucination Patient Simulator

* Structured patient case knowledge base (not free-form generation)
* Guardrails: response must be grounded in case data, "I don't know" for out-of-scope queries
* Hallucination detection: post-hoc verification each response against source case
* Target: <1% hallucination rate on clinical case queries
* File: `ai/platform/therapeutic_simulation_engine.py` (extend with guardrail layer)

### 2. Inquiry-Type Classification System

* Classify each therapist utterance into 1 of 4 types:
  * **Closed-ended**: Verification/fact-checking ("Do you sleep well?")
  * **Open-ended**: Exploratory/patient-led ("Tell me more about that")
  * **Guided**: Hypothesis-testing/channeled ("When you feel anxious, what thoughts come up?")
  * **Reflective**: Meta-cognitive/therapeutic ("How does that pattern show up elsewhere?")
* Implement classifier: rule-based (patterns + keywords) + LLM-as-judge for ambiguous cases
* Output: per-session inquiry type distribution with timestamps
* File: `ai/core/pipelines/quality/conversation_quality_pattern_analyzer.py`

### 3. Liebig's Law Diagnostic Quality Metrics

* Compute inquiry-type distribution vectors per session
* Infer "bottleneck" skills: if open-ended ratio < 15%, diagnosis-limited by exploration
* Quality score: min(inquiry_type_scores) — the weakest skill determines overall score
* Visualize as radar chart: 4 axes (one per inquiry type) + diagnosis accuracy
* Track across sessions to identify therapist skill gaps
* File: `ai/core/pipelines/quality/conversation_quality_pattern_analyzer.py`

### 4. Automated Diagnostic Quality Report

* Generate structured report per evaluation session including:
  * Inquiry distribution (counts + percentages per type)
  * Bottleneck analysis (which inquiry type is limiting accuracy)
  * Diagnosis accuracy comparison: with vs without full inquiry chain
  * Recommendations: which inquiry skills to develop
* Session comparison over time to track improvement
* File: `ai/evals/conversation_eval_metrics.py`

### 5. Controlled Comparison Study

* Replicate the Inquiry-Diagnosis paper's experiment: evaluate diagnostic ability WITH vs WITHOUT patient simulator
* Test: naive prompt → diagnosis accuracy vs structured simulation → diagnosis accuracy
* Measure: hallucination rate, diagnosis accuracy, information completeness
* Document results: confirm paper's 12x hallucination reduction or note delta

### 6. Hallucination Detection System

* Implement `HallucinationDetector` that cross-checks each simulator response against source case data
* Detection methods: factual consistency, temporal consistency, numerical accuracy, scope compliance
* Alert on hallucination with severity grading, log for analysis
* File: `ai/core/pipelines/quality/conversation_quality_pattern_analyzer.py`

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Hallucination rate < 1% on test set of 200 clinical queries
- [ ] Inquiry-type classifier achieves 90%+ accuracy on labeled test set
- [ ] Liebig bottleneck analysis correctly identifies limiting inquiry skill in 80%+ cases
- [ ] Automated report generates within 30s per session
- [ ] Replication study confirms 5x+ hallucination reduction vs prompt-only baseline
- [ ] Integration with Therapeutic Simulation Engine (Patient-Ψ epic) for combined pipeline

## Dependencies

* `ai/platform/therapeutic_simulation_engine.py` — Patient-Ψ simulation engine
* `ai/core/pipelines/quality/conversation_quality_pattern_analyzer.py` — existing quality analysis
* `ai/evals/conversation_eval_metrics.py` — evaluation metrics

issues.title: [DeepRare] Multi-Agent Rare Disease Diagnosis Architecture
issues.description:
## Overview

Implement a multi-agent diagnostic architecture inspired by DeepRare (arXiv 2506.20430) which achieves **57.18% Recall@1** across 2,919 rare diseases — **23.79% absolute improvement** over the second-best method. The architecture uses a 3-tier agent system with centralized orchestration, enabling structured clinical reasoning for rare disease diagnosis.

## Key Research Findings

* **Paper**: DeepRare: An Agentic Approach to Rare Disease Diagnosis (arXiv 2506.20430)
* **3-Tier Architecture**: Central Controller + Sub-agents (Symptom Analyzer, Test Interpreter, Literature Matcher) + Knowledge Retrieval
* **Benchmark**: 57.18% Recall@1 on 2,919 rare diseases across 16 organ systems
* **57.18% vs 33.39%** (second-best) — dominant improvement margin
* Key insight: Rare diseases require structured reasoning + external knowledge retrieval, not just parametric knowledge

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. Central Controller Agent (`ControllerOrchestrator`)

* Receives patient case, decomposes into sub-tasks for sub-agents
* Maintains differential diagnosis list with probability weights
* Decides when to request additional tests / specialist consultation
* Convergence criteria: when top-5 list stabilizes across 3 iterations OR all sub-agents agree
* Implements `RareDiseaseState` with: active_hypotheses, eliminated_conditions, pending_inquiries, evidence_strength
* File: `ai/platform/pixelated_empathy_core.py` (extend multi-agent framework)

### 2. Symptom Analyzer Sub-Agent

* Maps symptoms to rare disease phenotype patterns
* Identifies: pathognomonic symptoms (high specificity), symptom clusters, temporal progression patterns
* Extracts structured symptom profiles: onset, duration, severity, progression, associated factors
* Uses rare disease ontology mapping (ORPHA, OMIM) — integrate existing medical ontology if available
* Output: structured symptom-disease probability matrix

### 3. Test Interpreter Sub-Agent

* Interprets lab results, imaging findings, genetic tests
* Maps findings to disease-specific diagnostic criteria
* Requests additional tests when differential remains broad (>5 conditions)
* Implements Bayesian test-result updating: P(Disease | TestResult) calculation

### 4. Literature Matcher Sub-Agent

* Retrieves relevant literature / case reports matching patient profile
* Uses hybrid search (semantic + keyword) against rare disease knowledge base
* Returns: matching case reports, suggested diagnostic criteria, treatment implications
* Priority: most similar presentations first, with similarity score transparency

### 5. Knowledge Retrieval Layer

* Structured rare disease knowledge base with: disease profiles, diagnostic criteria, phenotypic spectra, treatment guidelines
* Supports fast lookups by symptom, gene, organ system, disease cluster
* Integration with external medical ontologies (HPO, ORPHA, OMIM)
* Interface: `RareDiseaseKnowledgeBase` class with hybrid retrieval (semantic + keyword + structured query)

### 6. Differential Diagnosis Manager

* Maintains ranked differential list with evidence strength per condition
* Supports: Bayesian updating, likelihood ratio calculations, evidence accumulation
* Implements pruning: eliminate conditions with <1% posterior probability
* Convergence detection: when top-3 unchanged for 3 iterations
* Output: ranked differential with supporting evidence for each condition

### 7. DiagnosisArena Evaluation Adapter

* Reuse DiagnosisArena evaluation methodology for end-to-end assessment
* Metrics: Recall@1, Recall@5, Recall@10, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR)
* Report accuracy by organ system, disease rarity tier, presentation complexity
* Compare against single-agent baseline (no decomposition)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Central orchestrator correctly decomposes 10+ rare disease cases
- [ ] Symptom Analyzer correctly identifies pathognomonic patterns in 80%+ cases
- [ ] Test Interpreter reduces differential by 50%+ when tests available
- [ ] Literature Matcher retrieves relevant case reports for 90%+ rare diseases
- [ ] End-to-end Recall@1 >= 40% on held-out rare disease test set
- [ ] Performance: sub-60-second end-to-end per case
- [ ] Integration with existing `pixelated_empathy_core.py` architecture

## Dependencies

* `ai/platform/pixelated_empathy_core.py` — multi-agent framework extension
* `ai/core/pipelines/inference/rare_disease_pipeline.py` (to be created)
* Medical ontology resources (HPO, ORPHA, OMIM) — check `ai/data/` for existing
* DeepRare paper implementation reference for algorithm details

issues.title: [Patient-Ψ] CCD-Based Cognitive Patient Simulation Engine
issues.description:
## Overview

Implement a Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram (CCD)-driven patient simulation engine in `ai/platform/therapeutic_simulation_engine.py`, inspired by PATIENT-Ψ (arXiv 2405.19660). The paper demonstrates that injecting clinical psychology frameworks (CCD with 8 cognitive components) into LLM patient simulation achieves **0.87 anthropomorphism score** vs 0.31 for standard GPT-4 prompting — a 2.8x improvement.

## Key Research Findings

* **Paper**: PATIENT-Ψ: Using LLMs to Simulate Patients for CBT Training (arXiv 2405.19660)
* **Benchmark**: 0.87 anthropomorphism score, 0.67 narrative consistency (human-level)
* **Mechanism**: CCD provides structured patient architecture that LLMs naturally extend — no special training needed
* **6 Conversational Styles**: Resistant, Somatizing, Catastrophizing, Intellectualizing, Dependent, Open/Cooperative — each with distinct linguistic patterns
* **Cost**: ~$0.05/session with GPT-4o mini

## Implementation Tasks

### 1. CCD Schema & Data Structures

* Define 8 CCD components as Pydantic models: core_beliefs, intermediate_beliefs (attitudes/rules/assumptions), coping_strategies (compensation/avoidance/overcompensation), compensatory_strategies, situation_interpretation, emotional_response, behavioral_response, cognitive_triads
* Create CCD_PROFILES registry with ~15 base profiles (depression, GAD, social anxiety, PTSD, OCD, panic disorder, etc.)
* Each profile includes: primary diagnosis, core belief themes, typical coping patterns, cognitive distortion tendencies, comorbidity flags
* File: `ai/platform/therapeutic_simulation_engine.py`

### 2. CCD Injection Prompt Template

* Design prompt architecture that interleaves CCD components into system prompts
* Structured format: [PATIENT_IDENTITY] → [CCD_PROFILE] → [SITUATION_CONTEXT] → [CONVERSATIONAL_STYLE] → [HISTORY_SUMMARY]
* Include dynamic difficulty scaling (simple → complex presentations as training progresses)
* Ensure CCX compatibility with existing `pixel_inference_service.py` prompt pipeline

### 3. 6 Conversational Style Implementations

* **Resistant**: Minimal disclosure, deflection, challenging therapist competence — verbal/non-verbal markers
* **Somatizing**: Physical symptom focus, emotional → somatic translation patterns
* **Catastrophizing**: Worst-case scenario framing, probability overestimation markers
* **Intellectualizing**: Abstract/analytic language, emotional distancing patterns
* **Dependent**: Excessive reassurance seeking, helplessness framing
* **Open/Cooperative**: Balanced disclosure, collaborative language, insight-ready markers
* Each style needs: linguistic markers, response probability weights, escalation/de-escalation triggers

### 4. Dynamic State Machine

* Track session state across: engagement_level, resistance_level, therapeutic_alliance, insight_stage
* State transitions based on therapist interventions (reflection → alliance +, confrontation → resistance +)
* Implement `TherapySessionState` class with transition rules and state persistence
* Support multi-turn coherence: patient remembers prior disclosures, responds consistently
* File: `ai/platform/therapeutic_simulation_engine.py`

### 5. Multi-Turn Coherence System

* Maintain conversation history as structured episodic memory (not raw text)
* Key constraints: no contradicted facts, consistent emotional arc, therapy-stage-appropriate responses
* Implement `PatientMemory` with: episodic_buffer, belief_consistency_checker, emotional_arc_tracker
* Cross-check each response against established CCD profile before generation

### 6. API Integration

* Extend `TherapySimulationRequest` API schema with CCD profile selection, conversational style, difficulty level
* Add `POST /api/v1/therapy/simulate` endpoint
* Return structured session data: transcript, CCD state transitions, style adherence metrics
* Files: `ai/api/pixel_inference_service.py`, `ai/api/schemas/`

### 7. Validation Suite

* Anthropomorphism evaluation using GPT-4o-as-judge (replicate paper's methodology)
* Narrative consistency scoring across 5+ turns
* CCD profile adherence: does simulated behavior match profile predictions?
* Compare against baseline (prompt-only patient) — expect 2x+ improvement in anthropomorphism

## Success Criteria

- [ ] CCD schema supports 15+ clinical profiles with all 8 components
- [ ] All 6 conversational styles produce distinguishable interaction patterns
- [ ] Anthropomorphism score >= 0.80 (paper baseline: 0.87)
- [ ] State machine correctly models 5+ session-level state transitions
- [ ] Multi-turn coherence: no contradicted facts across 10+ turns
- [ ] API endpoint accepts structured parameters and returns parsed session data
- [ ] Integration tests pass for all style × profile combinations

## Dependencies

* Existing `ai/platform/therapeutic_simulation_engine.py` structure
* `ai/api/pixel_inference_service.py` for LLM inference calls
* `ai/core/pipelines/quality/conversation_quality_pattern_analyzer.py` for quality metrics

issues.title: refactor(memory): upstream StanceShift & SynthesisResult into @pixelated/memory-schema
issues.description:
## Context

Follow-up to [PIX-3890](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3890/replace-ad-hoc-unifiedmemory-definitions-in-srclibaimemorytypests-with), which rewrote `src/lib/ai/memory/types.ts` as a re-export barrel from `@pixelated/memory-schema` for `UnifiedMemory`, `EmotionalContext`, `EmpathyMetrics`, `GateResult`, and friends. Two types — `StanceShift` and `SynthesisResult` — were intentionally **left local** because they were not yet upstream in the package.

This left the barrel with a Foresight-specific carve-out:

```ts
// src/lib/ai/memory/types.ts (current state)
export type { /* ...package re-exports... */ } from '@pixelated/memory-schema'

// Foresight-specific — not yet upstream
export interface StanceShift { ... }
export interface SynthesisResult { ... }
```

## Goal

Move `StanceShift` and `SynthesisResult` (plus their Zod schemas and runtime guards) into `@pixelated/memory-schema` so `src/lib/ai/memory/types.ts` shrinks to a **pure re-export barrel** with zero Foresight-specific carve-outs.

## Scope

### In `packages/memory-schema/`

1. `src/types.ts` — add two new interfaces:

   `StanceShift` — detected change in user/persona behavior
   * `attribute: string` (e.g. `'openness'`, `'defensiveness'`)
   * `oldValue: number`
   * `newValue: number`
   * `delta: number`
   * `evidenceIds: string[]` — IDs of memories showing the shift
   * `confidence: number` (constrained `0.0 – 1.0`, matching package convention)

   `SynthesisResult` — output of a reconciliation pass
   * `mergedIds: string[]`
   * `newMemoryId: string`
   * `stanceShifts: StanceShift[]`
   * `compressionRatio: number` (constrained `0.0 – 1.0`)

   Field rename plan (snake_case → camelCase) verified against current local `types.ts`: `old_value`→`oldValue`, `new_value`→`newValue`, `evidence_ids`→`evidenceIds`, `merged_ids`→`mergedIds`, `new_memory_id`→`newMemoryId`, `stance_shifts`→`stanceShifts`, `compression_ratio`→`compressionRatio`. Matches the package's existing camelCase convention (`UnifiedMemory.synthesizedFrom`, `vectorId`, etc.).
2. `src/schemas.ts` — add `StanceShiftSchema` and `SynthesisResultSchema` (camelCase, matching the new interface names). `SynthesisResultSchema.stanceShifts` must reference the new `StanceShiftSchema`. Use `.min(0).max(1)` on `confidence` and `compressionRatio` for consistency with how `EmotionalContext` constrains its normalized floats.
3. `src/guards.ts` — add `isStanceShift` and `isSynthesisResult` type guards (structural — same pattern as `isUnifiedMemory`).
4. `src/index.ts` — export `StanceShift`, `SynthesisResult`, `StanceShiftSchema`, `SynthesisResultSchema`, `isStanceShift`, `isSynthesisResult`.
5. `MEMORY_SCHEMA_VERSION` — bump from `1.0.0` → `1.1.0`. **Rationale:** the package's own comment says "bump when adding fields to `UnifiedMemory`," which strictly would *not* require a bump for new top-level types. We're bumping anyway as a deliberate minor-version signal that the published schema surface grew, per semver. Document this choice in the package's CHANGELOG/PR description.
6. **Package README** — list `StanceShift` and `SynthesisResult` in the exported types table, if the package has one.

### In `src/lib/ai/memory/`

`types.ts` — delete the local `StanceShift` and `SynthesisResult` interface declarations. Replace with re-exports:

```ts
export type { StanceShift, SynthesisResult } from '@pixelated/memory-schema'
```

The file becomes a **pure** re-export barrel — no Foresight-specific types.

`synthesizer.ts` (consumer update — required, not optional) — currently constructs `StanceShift` and `SynthesisResult` values inline with snake_case keys (`merged_ids`, `new_memory_id`, `stance_shifts`, `old_value`, `new_value`, `evidence_ids`, `compression_ratio`). After the package types become camelCase, **all of these must be renamed** in `synthesizer.ts`. The [PIX-3890](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3890/replace-ad-hoc-unifiedmemory-definitions-in-srclibaimemorytypests-with) camelCase migration established this pattern; apply the same to the new fields. Any other file that constructs or reads these fields (`linker.ts`, `gate.ts`, etc.) needs the same treatment — check the codebase before claiming "no further consumer changes."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `StanceShift` and `SynthesisResult` interfaces live in `packages/memory-schema/src/types.ts`
- [ ] `StanceShiftSchema` and `SynthesisResultSchema` live in `packages/memory-schema/src/schemas.ts` with `.min(0).max(1)` constraints on `confidence` and `compressionRatio`
- [ ] `isStanceShift` and `isSynthesisResult` type guards live in `packages/memory-schema/src/guards.ts`
- [ ] All four are exported from `packages/memory-schema/src/index.ts`
- [ ] `MEMORY_SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped to `1.1.0` (with rationale documented in PR description)
- [ ] `src/lib/ai/memory/types.ts` contains **only** re-exports from `@pixelated/memory-schema` — no local interface declarations
- [ ] `src/lib/ai/memory/synthesizer.ts` updated to use camelCase fields for all `StanceShift` / `SynthesisResult` accessors (no `*.old_value`, `*.merged_ids`, `*.stance_shifts`, `*.compression_ratio`, etc. remain)
- [ ] Any other consumer of these types in `src/lib/ai/memory/` (linker, gate, index, tests) is updated and typechecks
- [ ] `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` on the memory module is clean
- [ ] All 11+ memory tests pass
- [ ] Package README (if present) lists the two new types

## Dependencies

**Lands after** [PIX-3890](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3890/replace-ad-hoc-unifiedmemory-definitions-in-srclibaimemorytypests-with) so the barrel can become a pure re-export — the work is technically independent (the package can hold the new types even if the local barrel still has its carve-out) but loses its meaning if done first, because [PIX-3890](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3890/replace-ad-hoc-unifiedmemory-definitions-in-srclibaimemorytypests-with) would have just re-exported them as part of the barrel. Doing [PIX-3890](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3890/replace-ad-hoc-unifiedmemory-definitions-in-srclibaimemorytypests-with) first also establishes the snake_case→camelCase migration pattern in the consumers.

**No upstream blockers** — package is in this monorepo, all files are local.

## Out of scope

* Adding `StanceShift` / `SynthesisResult` to the SQLite / MongoDB persistence layers (separate work; this ticket is type-only)
* Changing the existing `MemoryLinker.test.ts` / `MemorySystem.test.ts` fixtures (these types aren't constructed in tests)
* Refactoring the synthesizer logic itself — only type plumbing
* Adding a `buildSynthesisResult(...)` factory to `packages/memory-schema/src/defaults.ts` — would be nice for consistency with `buildMemorySkeleton`, but a follow-up consideration, not in this ticket

## Estimate

Small — ~80 lines added to the package, ~10 lines removed from local types, ~10–20 lines of consumer updates in `synthesizer.ts` and possibly elsewhere. Half-day at most.

issues.title: Add contract tests + OpenAPI spec that lock the v1 surface and document the product-only decision
issues.description:
## Context

The v1 contract is meant to be stable enough for future SDK and developer-platform  
work, but right now there is no automated test that proves the wire format  
matches the Zod schemas, and no OpenAPI spec that consumers can generate  
clients from. There is also no written decision explaining why the public API  
is product-only (no developer-platform access yet) and what would have to change  
to open it up. Without these, the next refactor will silently break consumers.

## Goal

Lock the v1 surface so that any unintended change to a request, response, or  
error shape fails CI. Publish a hand-written OpenAPI 3.1 spec for `/api/v1/memory/*`  
that mirrors the Zod schemas 1:1. Add a written decision record that codifies  
the product-only exposure rule and the path to opening it up.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New file `src/lib/memory/contract/__tests__/v1.contract.test.ts` that, for  
   each of the 5 operations, fetches the live `/api/v1/memory/*` route (with a  
   stubbed gateway) and asserts the response passes the corresponding response  
   Zod schema. Any future change to either the schema or the handler that  
   breaks the contract fails this test.
2. The same test suite also asserts that the legacy `/api/memory/*` shim  
   responses still pass the v1 schema (proving the shim is faithful) and that  
   the `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers are present.
3. New file `docs/api/memory-v1.openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1) that documents the  
   5 operations, the `MemoryError` schema, and the identity/scope envelope. The  
   spec is generated from the Zod schemas via a small script  
   (`scripts/generate-memory-openapi.ts`) checked into the repo, and the spec is  
   regenerated as part of `pnpm build:api-docs`.
4. New file `docs/api/memory-v1-decision.md` (Architecture Decision Record) that  
   records: (a) why v1 is product-only, (b) what the contract is and is not  
   allowed to do (no internal Hindsight/MCP leaks), (c) the criteria that would  
   justify opening it up to a developer platform, and (d) the deprecation  
   policy for v1 when v2 ships. The ADR is referenced from  
   `docs/api/memory-v1-contract.md`.
5. CI runs the contract test suite on every PR that touches  
   `src/lib/memory/contract/**` or `src/pages/api/v1/memory/**`. Lint and  
   typecheck stay clean.

## Related

* Parent: [PIX-1908](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-1908/define-the-canonical-public-memory-api-contract)
* Sibling (must land first): sub-tasks 1, 2, and 3 of [PIX-1908](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-1908/define-the-canonical-public-memory-api-contract) — the contract  
  tests, the OpenAPI spec, and the ADR all reference the v1 surface those  
  sub-tasks produce.
* Adjacent: [PIX-3888](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3888/resolve-q-get-vs-query-post-field-name-inconsistency-in-v1-search) (Done) — the q vs query fix; the contract test pins this  
  so it cannot regress.
* Files: `src/lib/memory/contract/__tests__/v1.contract.test.ts` (new),  
  `docs/api/memory-v1.openapi.yaml` (new), `docs/api/memory-v1-decision.md`  
  (new), `docs/api/memory-v1-contract.md` (updated with ADR link),  
  `scripts/generate-memory-openapi.ts` (new).

6. The `pnpm build:api-docs` script referenced in AC [#3](<https://github.com/daggerstuff/pixelated/issues/3>) is added to the root  
   `package.json` as part of this change, wired to run the new  
   `scripts/generate-memory-openapi.ts` script. Running it from a clean checkout  
   produces an identical `docs/api/memory-v1.openapi.yaml` to the checked-in copy  
   (no diff). The script is documented in the repo's build commands.

issues.title: Update MemoryApiClient + SDK to consume the v1 contract and target /api/v1/memory/*
issues.description:
## Context

`src/lib/memory/memory-api-client.ts` is the TS client used by the frontend and
by `src/lib/sdk/index.ts`. Today it defines its own request/response types that
shadow the v1 contract, and it targets `/api/memory/*` (the un-versioned
namespace). This is exactly the kind of drift the canonical contract is meant to
prevent: client and server can disagree on field names without a type error.

## Goal

The client and SDK import their types directly from `src/lib/memory/contract/v1.ts`
and call `/api/v1/memory/*` only. `ProductMemoryClient` (`src/lib/memory/product-memory-client.ts`)
is also updated so the frontend never calls the deprecated un-versioned routes.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `src/lib/memory/memory-api-client.ts` no longer declares its own request/response
   types. It re-exports the types from `@/lib/memory/contract` and its method
   signatures are typed against `z.infer` of the v1 schemas (e.g.
   `create(input: CreateMemoryRequest): Promise<CreateMemoryResponse>`).
2. All 5 operations are implemented on the client: `create`, `list`, `search`,
   `update(id, patch)`, `delete(id)`. `list` and `update` did not exist on the
   client before and are added here.
3. The base URL defaults to `/api/v1/memory` and the previous `/api/memory`
   prefix is no longer referenced anywhere in the client. A unit test asserts
   the base URL.
4. `src/lib/sdk/index.ts` re-exports the same client methods (and types) so the
   SDK is a thin pass-through; the SDK is no longer free to drift from the
   contract.
5. `src/lib/memory/product-memory-client.ts` (the in-app client used by the
   frontend) is also updated to call the v1 routes and to use the v1 types. Any
   call site that still references the old un-versioned routes is updated.
6. `src/lib/memory/__tests__/memory-api-client.test.ts` is updated to use the v1
   types and to assert that requests hit `/api/v1/memory/*`. All tests pass.

## Related

* Parent: PIX-1908
* Sibling (must land first or together): sub-tasks 1 and 2 of PIX-1908 (v1
  contract schemas + v1 routes) — the client cannot consume types that do not
  exist yet.
* Files: `src/lib/memory/memory-api-client.ts`,
  `src/lib/memory/product-memory-client.ts`,
  `src/lib/memory/__tests__/memory-api-client.test.ts`,
  `src/lib/sdk/index.ts`.

issues.title: Build the versioned /api/v1/memory/* public route layer that consumes the v1 contract
issues.description:
## Context

The current public surface lives at `/api/memory/*` (`src/pages/api/memory/create.ts`,  
`search.ts`, `delete.ts`). It already imports Zod schemas from the v1 contract,  
but: (a) there is no versioned URL prefix, (b) `list` and `update` operations are  
missing entirely, and (c) the route handlers hand-roll error envelopes instead of  
using the `MemoryError` schema. This means consumers cannot pin to a stable  
version and the SDK/docs have to track ad-hoc handler logic.

## Goal

Introduce `/api/v1/memory/*` as the versioned public namespace. Each route  
imports its request schema from `src/lib/memory/contract/v1.ts`, validates the  
incoming body/query with `.parse()` (returning a `MemoryError` on failure),  
delegates to the product-memory-gateway, and returns the v1 response shape  
verbatim. The legacy `/api/memory/*` routes are kept as thin shims that forward  
to the v1 handlers, and are marked deprecated in their response headers.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New route files exist: `src/pages/api/v1/memory/create.ts`,  
   `src/pages/api/v1/memory/list.ts`, `src/pages/api/v1/memory/search.ts`,  
   `src/pages/api/v1/memory/[id]/update.ts`,  
   `src/pages/api/v1/memory/[id]/delete.ts`. All import their request/response  
   schemas from `@/lib/memory/contract`.
2. Every handler runs `RequestSchema.parse(req.body ?? req.query)` and returns a  
   400 with `{ error: MemoryError }` (code `validation_failed`) on parse failure.
3. Every handler delegates to the product-memory-gateway via a single helper  
   (`withV1Contract(handler)`) that injects the identity/scope envelope, sets  
   `X-Contract-Version: 1` on the response, and converts thrown gateway errors  
   into the `MemoryError` shape.
4. The legacy `/api/memory/*` routes are reduced to one-liner shims that call the  
   v1 handler and add `Deprecation: true` + `Sunset` response headers pointing at  
   the v1 URL. They still pass `memory-routes.test.ts`.
5. New integration tests at `src/tests/api/v1/memory-routes.test.ts` cover the 5  
   operations end-to-end (happy path + 400 on bad input + 401 on missing  
   identity). All pass.
6. Typecheck clean, lint clean, no `any` introduced.

## Related

* Parent: [PIX-1908](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-1908/define-the-canonical-public-memory-api-contract)
* Sibling (must land first or together): sub-task 1 of [PIX-1908](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-1908/define-the-canonical-public-memory-api-contract) (the complete v1  
  contract schemas) — the routes import from it.
* Depends on: [PIX-3889](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3889/wire-pixelatedmemory-schema-into-the-product-memory-gateway) (gateway wired to @pixelated/memory-schema) so the  
  identity/scope envelope is real and the routes can call into it.
* Files: `src/pages/api/v1/memory/*`, `src/pages/api/memory/*` (shims),  
  `src/lib/memory/contract/v1.ts`, `src/lib/middleware/with-v1-contract.ts` (new).

6. The Deprecation response header on the legacy shim routes carries an explicit  
   removal date (Sunset header) that is no later than the GA of v2. The removal  
   date is documented in the ADR produced by [PIX-3904](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-3904/add-contract-tests-openapi-spec-that-lock-the-v1-surface-and-document).

issues.title: Complete the canonical v1 contract schemas (CRUD + error + identity/scope)
issues.description:
## Context

`src/lib/memory/contract/v1.ts` already defines Zod schemas for the v1 public
memory API and was the source of the `q` vs `query` field-name fix (PIX-3888,
Done). But it is still incomplete: it covers `search` fully, partially covers
`create`/`delete`, and is missing `list`/`update`. There is no formal error
contract, and the identity/scope fields (workspaceId, userId, role, scope) are
not consistently aligned with the workspace tenancy model that the
product-memory-gateway and the @pixelated/memory-schema package now use.

## Goal

Make `src/lib/memory/contract/v1.ts` the single source of truth for the public
memory API surface. Every public operation (create, list, search, update, delete)
has matching request/response Zod schemas, an explicit error contract, and the
canonical identity/scope fields used by the gateway.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `src/lib/memory/contract/v1.ts` exports Zod schemas for all 5 operations:
   `CreateMemoryRequest`, `ListMemoriesRequest` (with pagination cursor),
   `SearchMemoriesRequest`, `UpdateMemoryRequest`, `DeleteMemoryRequest`, plus
   matching `*Response` schemas. Schemas are inferred (`z.infer`) into TS types
   and re-exported from `src/lib/memory/contract/index.ts`.
2. An explicit `MemoryError` schema is exported: `{ code: enum<MemoryErrorCode>, message: string, details?: Record<string, unknown>, requestId?: string }`
   where `MemoryErrorCode` is a closed enum (e.g. `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
   `not_found`, `validation_failed`, `gate_blocked`, `rate_limited`,
   `internal_error`).
3. All request/response schemas include the canonical identity/scope envelope
   shared with the workspace model: `workspaceId`, `userId`, `scope` (enum
   `product` | `developer`), `role` (enum `owner` | `clinician` | `member` |
   `observer`). These are required for write operations, optional for read.
4. Schemas reject any extra fields by default (`.strict()` on every object) so
   the contract cannot silently drift. Tests assert that an extra key produces a
   `validation_failed` error.
5. Typecheck clean (`pnpm typecheck`) and the existing `memory-routes.test.ts`
   and `memory-api-client.test.ts` still pass after the additions.

## Related

* Parent: PIX-1908 (Define the canonical public memory API contract)

  identity/scope envelope matches what the gateway actually consumes.
* Adjacent: PIX-3891 (Zod schemas in @pixelated/memory-schema) — this sub-task
